# OpenMarkdown Editor: full documentation

> Every guide and the API reference of `@openmarkdown-dev/editor`, concatenated. Index: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/llms.txt

# OpenMarkdown Editor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/

`@openmarkdown-dev/editor` is a live-preview Markdown editor built on [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/).
Headings, lists, tables, math, Mermaid diagrams, callouts and YAML properties render in place,
and the Markdown shows under the caret. It edits the Markdown source text itself, for a
lossless round-trip: open and save without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was.
When you edit, only what you touched changes, with a few exceptions, each pinned by a test.

It is the editor inside the [OpenMarkdown](https://openmarkdown.dev) app, extracted as an MIT library.

## Start here

1. [Install](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/install/) the package and its CodeMirror peers.
2. [Mount your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/) in plain JavaScript.
3. Use it [in React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/) or [in any other framework](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/).

## Guides

- [The host: `EditorHost`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/host/): the per-document callbacks (changes, links, images, outline).
- [The environment: `EditorEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/): per editor or as page defaults (color scheme, clipboard, links, spelling, keys).
- [Embed in a form or CMS field](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/embed-in-a-form/): auto height, labels, a string value, read-only, image uploads, replacing a CodeMirror editor.
- [Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/): the `--ome-*` custom properties.
- [UI language](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/language/): English, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
- [Images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/): showing, pasting, dropping and resizing.
- [Markdown syntax](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/syntax/): what the editor renders, what it shows as written, and how math delimiters are read.
- [Untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/): what the editor does with a document written by someone else.
- [Server-side rendering](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/): importing on the server, mounting in the browser.
- [Self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/): building the editor into static files, without a bundler or a CDN, under a strict CSP.

## Fidelity

- [What the editor changes in your file](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/), and what it never changes.
- [How we compared it with other editors](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/method/): method, an example diff, the run date and the caveats.

## Reference and examples

- The [API reference](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/) is generated from the package's type declarations.
- [Examples](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/): small projects you can run, one per task.
- [Live demo](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/demo/): the editor with a showcase document.

## Code and app

The editor's source is in its public repository, and the same editor ships inside the
OpenMarkdown app for macOS, Windows and Linux. To see it with files, folders and an agent
around it, [get the app](https://openmarkdown.dev/#download) or
[try the whole app in your browser](https://openmarkdown.dev/demo).

# Install

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/install/

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor
```

npm 7 and later also install the editor's **peer dependencies**, CodeMirror and Lezer. With
another package manager, or to pin them yourself, install them explicitly:

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor @codemirror/state @codemirror/view @codemirror/commands \
  @codemirror/language @codemirror/lang-markdown @codemirror/lang-html \
  @codemirror/search @codemirror/autocomplete @lezer/common @lezer/highlight @lezer/markdown
```

## Why peers

Your page must hold exactly one copy of `@codemirror/state`. Two copies break CodeMirror:
extensions from one copy are not recognised by the other ("Unrecognized extension value").
Because CodeMirror is a peer, an app that already uses CodeMirror shares its copy with the
editor.

## What else comes with it

- `temml` (math) and `mermaid` (diagrams) are regular dependencies, declared as version ranges
  (`mermaid` `^11`), so an app that already has a Mermaid 11 shares its copy. The editor loads
  them with `import()` only when a document contains math or a diagram, and your bundler splits
  them into separate chunks. A document without either never downloads them.
- HTML inside Markdown is highlighted by `@codemirror/lang-html`, loaded the first time a
  document holds HTML; it is not part of the first load.
- There is no CSS file to import. The editor injects its styles, and every color and font is
  a `--ome-*` custom property you can override ([Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/)).

## Choose an entry

The package has three entries with the same API. They differ only in the renderers they carry
built in ([math and diagram renderers](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/)):

| Import | Formulas | Diagrams | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor` | Temml, built in | Mermaid, built in | You want everything to work out of the box. |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` | Temml, built in | yours, or none | No page needs diagrams, your page has its own Mermaid, or your style policy rules Mermaid out. |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-renderers` | yours, or none | yours, or none | Your page already renders math and diagrams (MathJax, KaTeX, Mermaid), or you bundle into one file. |

Nothing `/no-diagrams` imports reaches Mermaid, and nothing `/no-renderers` imports reaches Temml
or Mermaid, so your bundler emits no chunk for them, and a single-file (IIFE) bundle does not
inline them ([bundling into one file](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/bundling/)). npm still installs `mermaid` and
`temml`, the main entry's dependencies.

## Highlighted code blocks

Code blocks are highlighted when you opt in with `codeLanguages`. The usual list is
`@codemirror/language-data`'s (install it beside the editor; each language loads the first time a
block uses it):

```sh
npm install @codemirror/language-data
```

```ts
import { languages } from "@codemirror/language-data";
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({ doc, codeLanguages: languages });
```

Without it, fenced code shows unhighlighted and none of the twenty-odd `@codemirror/lang-*`
packages enter your lockfile.

## Release-age gates

Some projects refuse packages published in the last few days: bun's `minimumReleaseAge`
(`bunfig.toml`), pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`), or a CI policy built on
`npm install --before`. A version of the editor younger than that window is refused. The gate
falls back to an older version only inside your version range: with `^0.2.0` in `package.json`
and 0.2.0 the newest release, no version qualifies, and the install fails until 0.2.0 is older
than the window. Pin the newest version older than your window instead:

```sh
npm view @openmarkdown-dev/editor time --json
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor@<version>   # the newest one older than your window
```

To exclude the package from the gate instead, bun's `minimumReleaseAgeExcludes` takes exact
package names, not patterns: list `"@openmarkdown-dev/editor"` (and `"@openmarkdown-dev/css"` if
you use the stylesheets); `"@openmarkdown-dev/*"` matches nothing.

Every release is listed with its date in the [changelog](https://github.com/OpenMarkdown-dev/OpenMarkdown-editor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md),
and its peers and dependencies are declared as ranges, so an older editor version installs with
the CodeMirror your app already has.

## No bundler?

Framework-free is not build-free. The package is ES modules with bare imports
(`@codemirror/state`, …), which a browser cannot resolve on its own. A page without a bundler
has two ways:

- **The prebuilt browser file**, `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/browser` (`dist/browser.js`): one
  minified ES module with CodeMirror, Lezer and the formula renderer inside, for a
  `<script type="module">`. It is the `/no-diagrams` entry; for diagrams, give it your page's
  Mermaid ([renderers](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/)). It cannot share CodeMirror with your page, so
  `extensions` built from another copy of CodeMirror do not work with it.
- **Your own build**, served from your server: [self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/) gives the
  build script, for a server-rendered app with no bundler or a page that may not use a CDN.

## Requirements

- The package is ES2022 JavaScript with TypeScript declarations included.
- Importing it needs no DOM, so it is safe in server code ([SSR](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/)).
  Mounting an editor needs a browser DOM.
- Every build is tested by mounting, typing, rendering math and a diagram, and switching mode
  and scheme in headless Chromium, WebKit (Safari's engine) and Firefox.

Next: [your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/).

# Your first editor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/

Two calls make an editor: `createEditorState` builds one document, and `mountEditor` shows it
in an element. When the document is a file, two more read and write its bytes:

```html
<div id="editor" style="height: 480px"></div>
```

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

let file = openMarkdownFile(new Uint8Array(await (await fetch("/notes.md")).arrayBuffer()));
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc: file.text }));

const bytes = saveMarkdownFile(editor.getDoc(), file); // write these back
```

Give the parent element a height. The editor fills it and scrolls inside it. For an editor that
grows with its content instead, like a form field, pass `height: "auto"` (see
[Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/#height)).

Fetch the file as bytes (`arrayBuffer()`), not as text: `openMarkdownFile` keeps the file's BOM
and line endings, refuses bytes that are not UTF-8, and `saveMarkdownFile` gives back the
original bytes when nothing was edited. Decoding with `response.text()` first would already have
dropped the BOM and the line endings the save needs. See [Fidelity](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/) for what
they keep.

After a save, make the bytes you wrote the new baseline, so that `editor.getDoc() !== file.text`
means "unsaved edits":

```ts
file = openMarkdownFile(bytes);
```

## Highlighted code blocks

Fenced code is plain until you opt in. Install `@codemirror/language-data` and pass its
`languages` as `codeLanguages` (each language loads the first time a block uses it):

```ts
import { languages } from "@codemirror/language-data";

const state = createEditorState({ doc: file.text, codeLanguages: languages });
```

See [install](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/install/#highlighted-code-blocks) for what this adds to your lockfile.

## Read and write the document as a string

When there is no file, only text (a form field, local storage), give the editor a string. It
keeps the document as a string in `\n`, so `editor.getDoc()` is the text.

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc: localStorage.getItem("notes.md") ?? "# Notes\n",
  host: {
    // isUserEdit is false for setDoc and other programmatic changes.
    onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
      if (isUserEdit) localStorage.setItem("notes.md", doc);
    },
  },
});
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, state);

editor.getDoc(); // the current Markdown, as a string
editor.setDoc("# Replaced\n"); // new text, for example after the file changed on disk; scroll position kept
```

`host` holds the per-document callbacks. Every one is optional; see [the host](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/host/).

## Modes

```ts
editor.setMode("source"); // "live" | "source" | "reading"
editor.mode(); // "source"
editor.focus(); // setMode does not move focus
```

- `live` (the default) renders Markdown in place and shows the source under the caret.
- `source` is the plain text, colored.
- `reading` is rendered and read-only.

Switching mode keeps the document, the selection and the undo history. It does not move
focus: when a button of yours calls `setMode`, the focus stays on that button, so call
`editor.focus()` afterwards if the user should be able to type right away. To start in
another mode, pass `mode` to `createEditorState`.

To make the document read-only in every mode, pass `editable: false` (or call
`editor.setEditable(false)`). Reading mode alone still lets the reader tick a task checkbox;
`editable: false` does not.

## Commands

The handle runs the editor's own commands, so you need no CodeMirror import for them:

```ts
editor.undo(); // as Mod+Z; false when there was nothing to undo
editor.redo();
editor.openSearch(); // the find panel, as Mod+F
editor.isSearchOpen(); // true
editor.closeSearch();
editor.revealText("## Setup"); // select its first occurrence and scroll to it
```

## The environment: per editor, with page defaults

Capabilities that are not about the document, such as the color scheme, the clipboard and
external links, can be given to each editor (`createEditorState({ environment })`) or set once
for the whole page as defaults. The UI language is page-wide. Set the defaults before the
first editor mounts:

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const media = matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
configureEditorEnvironment({
  language: "en",
  colorScheme: {
    current: () => (media.matches ? "dark" : "light"),
    subscribe: (cb) => {
      const on = () => cb(media.matches ? "dark" : "light");
      media.addEventListener("change", on);
      return () => media.removeEventListener("change", on);
    },
  },
  copyText: (text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text),
});
```

Without it the editor is light, English, and has no clipboard, external-link or spelling
behaviour. See [the environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/).

## Clean up

```ts
editor.destroy(); // when the editor leaves the page
```

`destroy` removes the view and stops following the color scheme.

## Several documents in one view

One state is one document, with its undo history, folds and mode. A host with several
documents (tabs, for example) can keep one state each and swap them into one view:

```ts
editor.view.setState(otherState);
editor.syncAmbient(); // re-apply the current light or dark scheme
```

Next: [React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/), or [any other framework](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/).

# Use it in React

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/

There is no React wrapper to install. Mount the editor in an effect, and destroy it in the
effect's cleanup:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

export function MarkdownField({ value, onChange }: { value: string; onChange: (doc: string) => void }) {
  const parent = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const editor = useRef<MarkdownEditor | null>(null);
  const latest = useRef(onChange);
  latest.current = onChange;

  useEffect(() => {
    const state = createEditorState({
      doc: value,
      host: { onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => isUserEdit && latest.current(doc) },
    });
    editor.current = mountEditor(parent.current!, state);
    return () => editor.current?.destroy();
    // Mount once; later `value` changes are pushed in below.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (editor.current && editor.current.getDoc() !== value) editor.current.setDoc(value);
  }, [value]);

  return <div ref={parent} style={{ height: 480 }} />;
}
```

## Why it is written this way

- **Mount once.** Rebuilding the editor on every render would lose the caret, the selection
  and the undo history. The effect has no dependencies, and later `value` changes go in through
  `setDoc`.
- **Callbacks through a ref.** The editor reads `host` through the object on every call, so
  you can mutate it, or read the latest props through a ref as above, without rebuilding the
  state.
- **Only user edits go up.** `setDoc` is not a user edit, so `isUserEdit` keeps a `value`
  pushed in from props from being echoed back to `onChange`.
- **Options go to `createEditorState`.** Highlighted code blocks, for example, are an opt-in:
  `createEditorState({ doc: value, codeLanguages: languages, host })` with `languages` from
  `@codemirror/language-data` ([install](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/install/#highlighted-code-blocks)).
- **Strict Mode** runs the effect twice in development. `destroy` in the cleanup removes the
  first editor before the second mounts.

## Props that change: theme, read-only, keys

Options that can change while the editor lives have a setter on the handle, so a prop maps to
one effect. Each editor keeps its own values; two editors on one page can differ:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

export function NoteEditor({ doc, dark, readOnly, onSave }: { doc: string; dark: boolean; readOnly: boolean; onSave: () => void }) {
  const parent = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const editor = useRef<MarkdownEditor | null>(null);
  const save = useRef(onSave);
  save.current = onSave;

  useEffect(() => {
    editor.current = mountEditor(parent.current!, createEditorState({ doc, editable: !readOnly }));
    return () => editor.current?.destroy();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => editor.current?.setEditable(!readOnly), [readOnly]);
  useEffect(() => {
    editor.current?.setEnvironment({
      colorScheme: dark ? "dark" : "light",
      handleKey: (_view, e) => {
        if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "s") {
          save.current();
          return true;
        }
        return false;
      },
    });
  }, [dark]);

  return <div ref={parent} style={{ height: 480 }} />;
}
```

`setEnvironment` replaces this editor's own environment (members you leave out fall back to the
page's defaults from `configureEditorEnvironment`), and a new color scheme applies at once. See
[the environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/).

## Next.js and other server renderers

Importing the package on the server is safe, and the effect only runs in the browser, so the
component above works in a server-rendered page as it is. See [SSR](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/).

# Use it in any framework

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/

The editor is plain TypeScript and DOM. Any framework that gives you an element after it is in
the page, and a hook for when it leaves, can host it. The pattern is always the same:

1. When the element is mounted, call `createEditorState` and `mountEditor`.
2. When the element is removed, call `editor.destroy()`.
3. Send changes up from `host.onChange`. Push outside changes in with `editor.setDoc`, only when
   they differ from `editor.getDoc()`.

## Vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, onBeforeUnmount, ref, watch } from "vue";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const props = defineProps<{ modelValue: string }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{ "update:modelValue": [doc: string] }>();
const el = ref<HTMLDivElement>();
let editor: MarkdownEditor | null = null;

onMounted(() => {
  const state = createEditorState({
    doc: props.modelValue,
    host: { onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => isUserEdit && emit("update:modelValue", doc) },
  });
  editor = mountEditor(el.value!, state);
});
watch(() => props.modelValue, (doc) => {
  if (editor && editor.getDoc() !== doc) editor.setDoc(doc);
});
onBeforeUnmount(() => editor?.destroy());
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" style="height: 480px" />
</template>
```

## Svelte

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from "svelte";
  import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

  export let doc = "";
  let el: HTMLDivElement;

  onMount(() => {
    const editor = mountEditor(el, createEditorState({
      doc,
      host: { onChange: (next, isUserEdit) => { if (isUserEdit) doc = next; } },
    }));
    return () => editor.destroy();
  });
</script>

<div bind:this={el} style="height: 480px"></div>
```

## Web component

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type MarkdownEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

class MarkdownEditorElement extends HTMLElement {
  private editor: MarkdownEditor | null = null;

  connectedCallback() {
    const state = createEditorState({
      doc: this.textContent ?? "",
      host: {
        onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
          if (isUserEdit) this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("change", { detail: doc }));
        },
      },
    });
    this.textContent = "";
    this.editor = mountEditor(this, state);
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.editor?.destroy();
    this.editor = null;
  }
}
customElements.define("markdown-editor", MarkdownEditorElement);
```

## A plain `<script>` tag

Without a bundler, load the package and its peers from a CDN that resolves bare imports, for
example [esm.sh](https://esm.sh):

```html
<div id="editor" style="height: 480px"></div>
<script type="module">
  import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "https://esm.sh/@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

  mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor"), createEditorState({ doc: "# Hello\n" }));
</script>
```

# The host: `EditorHost`

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/host/

`EditorHost` is what the editor calls back into, for one document. Pass it as `host` to
`createEditorState`. Every callback is optional: leave one out and that feature is switched off
quietly. Nothing errors, and the rest of the editor carries on.

```ts
import { createEditorState, type EditorHost } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const host: EditorHost = {
  onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
    if (isUserEdit) save(doc);
  },
  resolveImage: (src) => (src.startsWith("https://") ? src : null),
};
const state = createEditorState({ doc, docPath: "/notes/today.md", host });
```

| Callback | Called when | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onChange(doc, isUserEdit, docPath)` | The document changed. `isUserEdit` is false for `setDoc` and other programmatic changes. | Nothing happens. |
| `resolveImage(src)` | An image is shown. Return a URL the page may load, or `null` to show the source. Script-capable URLs are dropped whatever you return. | Only absolute `https:` images load, from any host. Pass `() => null` to load none ([images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/)). |
| `openLink(absPath, fragment)` | A link to a local file was followed (Cmd/Ctrl+click; a plain click in reading mode). `fragment` is its `#fragment` without the `#`, or `null`. | Local links do nothing. |
| `getFolder()` | Link completion needs the root of the user's files. | Completion uses the document's own directory. |
| `listFiles(root)` | Link completion lists linkable files under `root` (root-relative paths). | Completion offers headings only. |
| `saveAttachment(docPath, bytes, hint)` | An image is pasted or dropped into a document with a path. Store it beside the document and resolve the relative path to link, or `null`. | `uploadImage` is used, if given. |
| `uploadImage(bytes, hint)` | An image is pasted or dropped, with or without a document path. Store it wherever you keep images and resolve the URL or path to link, or `null`. Used when the document has no path, or there is no `saveAttachment`. | Pasting or dropping an image inserts nothing (unless `saveAttachment` applies). |
| `onUnsupportedPaste(reason, count)` | Images were pasted or dropped but could not be stored: `reason` is `"no-save-attachment"` (neither saver) or `"no-doc-path"` (only `saveAttachment`, and no path). A notice only; nothing was inserted. | The images are dropped silently. |
| `onMoved()` | The selection or scroll position moved (debounced). Use it to remember the position. | Nothing happens. |
| `onOutline(items)` | The heading outline changed (`OutlineItem[]`, or `null` when the view goes away). | Nothing happens. |

## The host is read on every call

The editor keeps the object, not its functions, and reads the member each time it needs one.
You can mutate the object after creating the state, or forward to the latest props through a
ref ([React](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/react/)), without rebuilding the state.

## `docPath`

`docPath` is the document's absolute path, or `null` for an unsaved document. Relative links and
image paths resolve against its directory, and `saveAttachment` is only called when there is a
path to store beside (`uploadImage` needs none). Change it after a rename with `editor.setDocPath(path)`; read it with
`editor.docPath()`.

The path does not have to be a file on disk. A web app can use any absolute, `/`-separated name
(for example `/doc.md`) and resolve images in `resolveImage` from its own storage. See
[Images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/).

## Reading and writing the file

The editor works on a string; the file on disk is bytes. Decode it with `openMarkdownFile` and
encode `editor.getDoc()` with `saveMarkdownFile`, typically in `onChange` or on a save command:

```ts
import { createEditorState, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const file = openMarkdownFile(bytes); // throws InvalidUtf8Error for a file that is not UTF-8
const state = createEditorState({
  doc: file.text,
  host: {
    onChange: (doc, isUserEdit) => {
      if (isUserEdit) writeFile(saveMarkdownFile(doc, file));
    },
  },
});
```

Unedited, the bytes written are the bytes read; edited, the file keeps its BOM and its dominant
line ending. See [Fidelity](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/).

A host that holds the file as a string (a CMS field, a JSON API) uses `openMarkdownText` and
`saveMarkdownText` instead: the same reading of the BOM and line endings, on a string. For an
unsaved-changes indicator, `editor.isUnedited(file)` tells whether the document is still the
file's text, with the test the save functions use.

## Capabilities that are not about the document

The color scheme, the clipboard, external links, spelling, the UI language and host key
bindings belong to the editor environment: per editor through `createEditorState({ environment })`,
with page defaults from `configureEditorEnvironment`. See [the environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/).

The full signatures are in the [API reference](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorhost/).

# The environment: `EditorEnvironment`

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/

Some capabilities are not about a document: the color scheme, the clipboard, external links,
spelling, the UI language and the host's key bindings. Each editor can have its own, and the
page can set defaults that every editor uses for what it was not given:

- **Per editor:** pass `environment` to `createEditorState`, and change it later with
  `editor.setEnvironment(...)`. Two editors on one page can have different color schemes,
  link policies and key bindings.
- **Page defaults:** `configureEditorEnvironment(...)`, once, before the first editor mounts. A
  later call replaces the whole set. The UI `language` is page-wide and is only set here.

A member an editor's own environment gives replaces the page's for that editor; one it leaves
out falls back to the page's. Give a member as `undefined` to switch the page's off for one
editor.

Every member is optional. With neither, the editor is light, English, and has no clipboard,
external-link, spelling or host-key behaviour.

| Member | What it does | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | The editor's own UI words: `"en"`, `"zh"`, `"ja"` or `"ko"`. Page-wide only. | English. |
| `colorScheme` | `"light"` or `"dark"`, or a live source `{ current(), subscribe(cb) }` that the editor follows while it is mounted. | Always light. |
| `copyText(text)` | Put text on the clipboard (the code-block copy button). | No copy button action. |
| `openExternal(url)` | A web link was followed (Cmd/Ctrl+click; a plain click in reading mode). Your policy decides how it opens. | Web links do nothing. |
| `refusedLink(url, scheme)` | The editor refused a script-capable link (`javascript:`, `data:` and similar). Use it to tell the user. Never open the URL. | The refusal is silent. |
| `spell` | A `SpellService` that draws spelling squiggles and offers suggestions. | No spell checking. |
| `handleKey(view, event)` | Sees each key before the editor's defaults. Return `true` to consume it. | The editor's keymap only. |
| `renderMath(tex, displayMode)` | Your formula renderer (MathJax, KaTeX) in place of the built-in one; returns MathML ([renderers](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/)). | The entry's built-in Temml; with `/no-renderers`, formulas show as TeX. |
| `renderDiagram(source, scheme)` | Your diagram renderer (your page's Mermaid) in place of the built-in one; returns SVG ([renderers](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/)). | The main entry's built-in Mermaid; with the other entries, fences stay code. |

## One editor's own environment

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const editor = mountEditor(
  document.getElementById("comment")!,
  createEditorState({
    doc: "",
    environment: {
      colorScheme: "dark",
      openExternal: (url) => window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener"),
    },
  }),
);

// Later, when your theme prop changes:
editor.setEnvironment({ colorScheme: "light", openExternal: (url) => window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener") });
```

`setEnvironment` replaces the editor's own environment as a whole: pass every member you want
it to keep. The environment travels with the state, like the mode.

## Follow the system color scheme

As a page default, for every editor:

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const media = matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)");
configureEditorEnvironment({
  colorScheme: {
    current: () => (media.matches ? "dark" : "light"),
    subscribe: (cb) => {
      const on = () => cb(media.matches ? "dark" : "light");
      media.addEventListener("change", on);
      return () => media.removeEventListener("change", on);
    },
  },
  copyText: (text) => navigator.clipboard.writeText(text),
  openExternal: (url) => window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener"),
});
```

A mounted editor subscribes while it shows its state and unsubscribes in `destroy`. A page with
its own theme toggle implements `colorScheme` over that toggle, or passes a fixed `"light"` /
`"dark"` and calls `editor.setEnvironment` when the toggle changes.

## Spelling: `SpellService`

The editor draws its own spelling squiggles and suggestion menu; the checking is yours. A
`SpellService` has six members:

| Member | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `isOn()` | Is spell checking on right now? |
| `onChange(cb)` | Follow the on / off state. Returns the unsubscribe. |
| `newDocument()` | A fresh spell-document number for one editor, so a checker can keep per-editor ignore lists. |
| `check(doc, paragraphs)` | The misspellings (`SpellMiss`, UTF-16 `from` / `to` offsets) for each paragraph, in order, or `null` when the check could not run. |
| `suggestions(doc, paragraph, from, to)` | Up to five suggestions for `paragraph.slice(from, to)`. |
| `closeDocument(doc)` | The editor of `doc` is gone. |

Pass `checkSpelling: false` to `createEditorState` for an editor that should never show
squiggles, such as a small comment box.

## Host key bindings

`handleKey` sees every key the editor's keymap sees, before CodeMirror's defaults. Return `true`
when your binding ran. Give it per editor when each editor saves somewhere else:

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc,
  environment: {
    handleKey: (view, event) => {
      if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key === "s") {
        save(view.state.doc.toString());
        return true;
      }
      return false;
    },
  },
});
```

The full signatures are in the [API reference](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/).

# Embed in a form or CMS field

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/embed-in-a-form/

A Markdown field in a form, a CMS entry or a settings page differs from a full-page editor in a
few ways: it grows with its text, it has a label, its value is a string, it may be read-only,
and there is no file path to store pasted images beside. Each has an option.

## A complete field

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, openMarkdownText, saveMarkdownText } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const textarea = document.querySelector<HTMLTextAreaElement>("textarea[name=body]")!;
const file = openMarkdownText(textarea.value); // keeps the BOM and line endings it came with

const editor = mountEditor(
  document.getElementById("body-editor")!,
  createEditorState({
    doc: file.text,
    height: "auto", // as tall as its text; the page scrolls
    id: "body", // <label for="body"> focuses it
    ariaLabelledBy: "body-label", // and names it for screen readers
    host: {
      onChange: (doc) => {
        textarea.value = saveMarkdownText(doc, file); // what the form submits
      },
      uploadImage: async (bytes, hint) => upload(bytes, hint), // resolves a URL, or null
    },
  }),
);

document.getElementById("discard")!.addEventListener("click", () => {
  if (!editor.isUnedited(file)) editor.setDoc(file.text);
});
```

```html
<label id="body-label" for="body">Body</label>
<div id="body-editor" class="field"></div>
<textarea name="body" hidden></textarea>
```

```css
.field .ome-root { min-height: 12rem; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 6px; }
```

Style the field through `.ome-root`, never `.cm-editor`: a table cell being edited is an editor
of its own (`.ome-nested`), and a rule on `.cm-editor` would reach it too. To take the page's
font, size and color, use the "Fit the host page" recipe in [Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/).

## Height

`height: "auto"` makes the editor as tall as its content, with the bottom space the same as the
top (`--ome-padding-y`) instead of the room a full-page editor leaves to scroll past the end. A
`min-height` on `.ome-root` keeps an empty field from collapsing, and a click in the blank below
the text puts the caret at the end. The default, `"fill"`, takes the parent's height and
scrolls inside it. See [Theming](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/#height).

## Label, name and focus

The editable text is a `contenteditable` element, not a form control, so a browser does not
connect it to a `<label>` by itself:

- `id` puts the id on the editable text, and a click on a `<label for>` with that id focuses
  the editor.
- `ariaLabelledBy` (an element's id) or `ariaLabel` (a string) gives the field its accessible
  name. A `<label for>` alone does not name it for screen readers.
- `editor.focus()` gives it the keyboard focus, for example when a form shows a validation
  error.

## The value is a string

`openMarkdownText` and `saveMarkdownText` are the string form of the file codec: unedited, the
string you saved is the string you loaded, exactly; edited, it keeps the original BOM and line
endings. `editor.isUnedited(file)` answers "are there unsaved changes?" with the same test. If
you decode bytes yourself, decode with `TextDecoder("utf-8", { ignoreBOM: true })` (a default
decoder drops the BOM before the codec sees it), or pass the bytes to `openMarkdownFile`.

After a save, make what you saved the new baseline (`file = openMarkdownText(saved)`), so that
`isUnedited` means "unsaved since the last save".

## Read-only

`editable: false` makes the field read-only in every mode: no typing, pasting, dropping,
checkbox ticking or property editing, and no editing controls are drawn. The reader can still
select, copy, search and follow links. Switch it with `editor.setEditable(true | false)`, for
example while the form is submitting. Reading mode (`mode: "reading"`) is a different thing: a
rendered view that still lets the reader tick a task checkbox.

## Images without a file path

A CMS entry has no path, so `saveAttachment` (which stores an image beside the document) does
not apply. `uploadImage(bytes, hint)` stores the image wherever you keep images and resolves the
link target, or `null` when the upload failed. See [Images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/).

## Several fields on one page

Each editor has its own options. Give one field its own color scheme, link policy or key
bindings with `environment`, and change them with `editor.setEnvironment`; the page defaults
from `configureEditorEnvironment` fill in what a field does not give. See
[the environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/).

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc: "",
  environment: {
    handleKey: (_view, e) => {
      if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key === "Enter") {
        form.requestSubmit(); // Mod+Enter submits this field's form
        return true;
      }
      return false;
    },
  },
});
```

## Commands for a toolbar

A field's own toolbar can call the editor's commands on the handle, with no import from the
CodeMirror packages: `editor.undo()`, `editor.redo()`, `editor.openSearch()`,
`editor.closeSearch()`, `editor.isSearchOpen()`, `editor.revealText(text)` (select a passage
and scroll to it) and `editor.focus()`. `editor.view` is the CodeMirror view, for anything else.

## Class components and other lifecycles

The editor needs only a mount point and a cleanup. In a React class component, mount in
`componentDidMount`, call `editor.destroy()` in `componentWillUnmount`, and push outside value
changes in `componentDidUpdate` with `editor.setDoc(value)` when it differs from
`editor.getDoc()`. The same three steps fit any framework; see
[Use it in any framework](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/any-framework/).

## Replacing a CodeMirror editor you already have

If the field was a plain CodeMirror 6 editor, pass its state as `fromState`. The new editor takes
its document, selection and undo history, so Mod+Z still undoes what the user typed before the
switch:

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const previous = oldView.state; // built with history() from @codemirror/commands
oldView.destroy();
const editor = mountEditor(container, createEditorState({ fromState: previous, height: "auto" }));
```

The history carries over only when both editors use the same copy of `@codemirror/commands`
(it is a peer dependency, so one copy is the normal case). Nothing else of the old state comes
along: its extensions, keymaps and listeners are its own. Pass your own extensions again with
`extensions`, which takes one extension or an array.

# Theming

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/theming/

The editor paints only with `--ome-*` custom properties: colours, fonts, the type size,
the line height, the text column's width and the space around it. Each one has a light and
a dark default, and the editor switches between them with the environment's `colorScheme`
([environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/)). There is no CSS file to import.

## Where to put your styles

The editor's root element has the class **`.ome-root`**. Put your tokens, and any layout
rule of your own such as a border or a `min-height`, on that class:

```css
.ome-root {
  --ome-bg: #fffdf7;
  --ome-accent: #0b6bcb;
  --ome-font: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}
```

Setting tokens on `:root` has no effect. The editor declares its defaults on `.ome-root`
at zero specificity, so any selector that targets `.ome-root` wins, and an inherited value
does not.

Do not select `.cm-editor`. While a table cell or a property value is being edited, the
editor puts a second, small editor inside it, and that one is a `.cm-editor` too. A rule
such as `.my-field .cm-editor { min-height: 320px }` also lands on the cell's editor and
stretches its table row. The nested editor's root has the class **`.ome-nested`** and
never `.ome-root`, so a rule on `.ome-root` cannot reach it. It takes the root's token
values by inheritance: you do not need to style it.

These two classes and the `data-ome-scheme` attribute below are the editor's public
styling hooks. Every other class name inside the editor is internal and may change
between versions.

## Light and dark

The editor's root carries `data-ome-scheme="light"` or `data-ome-scheme="dark"`, and it
changes when the environment's `colorScheme` does. Give each scheme its own values with
that attribute:

```css
.ome-root[data-ome-scheme="light"] { --ome-accent: #0b6bcb; }
.ome-root[data-ome-scheme="dark"] { --ome-accent: #6cb6ff; }
```

This attribute is the one supported way to tell the schemes apart. CodeMirror's own light
and dark classes are generated names that change between builds, so do not select on them.

## Tokens

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--ome-bg` | The document surface: the editor's background, and the find bar's and menus'. |
| `--ome-fg` | Body text and the caret: the editor's text color. |
| `--ome-muted` | Quiet surfaces. |
| `--ome-muted-fg` | Secondary text: Markdown marks, placeholders, resting controls. |
| `--ome-border` | Hairlines: table rules, quote bars, frames. |
| `--ome-accent` | Links, selection, find hits, focus, list marks. |
| `--ome-danger` | Errors, such as a search with no match. |
| `--ome-agent` | The `@agent` mention. |
| `--ome-spelling` | The spelling squiggle. |
| `--ome-code-bg` | Inline code, code blocks, table headers (translucent). |
| `--ome-callout-note`, `--ome-callout-tip`, `--ome-callout-important`, `--ome-callout-warning`, `--ome-callout-caution` | The five callout kinds. |
| `--ome-state-hover`, `--ome-state-selected` | Hover and selected layers on controls. |
| `--ome-radius` | The corner radius of controls. |
| `--ome-font`, `--ome-font-mono` | The prose and code font stacks. No font files are shipped. |
| `--ome-font-size` | The body text size (default `16px`). Headings, code and everything else in the document are sized relative to it. |
| `--ome-line-height` | The body line height (default `1.7`). |
| `--ome-content-width` | The text column's maximum width (default `41rem`). `100%` makes it as wide as the editor. |
| `--ome-padding-x` | The space between the editor's left and right edges and the text column (default `2.5rem`). Fold toggles for headings and list items sit in it. |
| `--ome-padding-y` | The space above the first line (default `2rem`), and below the last one when the editor grows with its content. |
| `--ome-syntax-keyword`, `--ome-syntax-string`, `--ome-syntax-number`, `--ome-syntax-function`, `--ome-syntax-type`, `--ome-syntax-property` | Code highlighting. One value is used for both schemes. |

## Fit the host page

By default the editor brings its own look: an off-white surface, a centred 41rem column
and its own fonts. To make it look like part of your page instead, take your page's text
settings and let the column fill the editor:

```css
.ome-root {
  --ome-bg: #ffffff; /* your page's background colour */
  --ome-fg: inherit;
  --ome-font: inherit;
  --ome-font-size: inherit;
  --ome-line-height: inherit;
  --ome-content-width: 100%;
  --ome-padding-x: 1.5rem;
  --ome-padding-y: 0.75rem;
}
```

`inherit` on a token means "use the page's value": the editor then takes the text color,
font, size and line height of the element you mounted it in. This works as long as no
ancestor of the editor sets that `--ome-*` token itself.

Give `--ome-bg` your page's actual background colour rather than `transparent`: the find
bar and the editor's menus are painted with it, and a transparent one would let the text
show through them. Keep `--ome-padding-x` at about `1.5rem` if you want the fold toggles
next to headings and list items; with `0` they sit outside the editor's edge.

## Height

By default the editor fills its parent and scrolls inside it, so give the parent a height.
Below the last line it leaves room to scroll that line up to a comfortable reading height.

For an editor that grows with its content, like a form field or a comment box, pass
`height: "auto"` when you create the state:

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("field")!, createEditorState({ doc: "", height: "auto" }));
```

The editor is then as tall as its text, the page scrolls instead of the editor, and the
space below the last line is `--ome-padding-y`, the same as above the first. The parent
needs no height. To keep an empty editor from collapsing, give it a minimum height:

```css
.ome-root {
  min-height: 12rem;
}
```

A click anywhere in that minimum height places the caret, as a click below the text does
in a full-height editor.

## Beyond tokens

Anything the tokens do not cover can be styled with CodeMirror's own theme extensions, passed
through `extensions` on `createEditorState`. Class names inside the editor are not part of the
public API and may change between versions; the tokens, `.ome-root`, `.ome-nested` and
`data-ome-scheme` are.

# UI language

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/language/

The editor draws a few words of its own: the find panel, the copy and fold buttons, the
properties block, and image and link chips. They ship in four languages:

| Code | Language |
| --- | --- |
| `"en"` | English (the default) |
| `"zh"` | Chinese (Simplified) |
| `"ja"` | Japanese |
| `"ko"` | Korean |

Choose one with the environment, before the first editor mounts:

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

configureEditorEnvironment({ language: "ja" });
```

- The editor does not guess from the browser. Without `language`, or with a code it does not
  ship, it speaks English, so it behaves the same in every host and your app stays the one place
  that decides the language.
- The language is read when a word is drawn. Words already on screen do not redraw when you call
  `configureEditorEnvironment` again; mount the editor again (or reload) to switch a live page.
- Your document text can be in any language. Only the editor's own controls are translated.
  CJK text and emoji are edited and measured as written (table columns count them as two
  columns wide).

# Images

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/

The editor shows Markdown images (`![alt](src)`) in place, lets the user paste or drop new ones,
and resizes them with a drag. Where image bytes come from and where they go is the host's
decision, through `EditorHost` callbacks.

## Showing images: `resolveImage`

`resolveImage(src)` gets the image target exactly as written and returns a URL the page may load,
or `null` to show the source text instead.

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc,
  docPath: "/notes/today.md",
  host: {
    resolveImage: (src) => {
      if (src.startsWith("https://")) return src;
      return `/files/notes/${src.replace(/^\.\//, "")}`; // your server serves the document's folder
    },
  },
});
```

- Without `resolveImage`, absolute `https:` images load, from any host, and nothing else does.
  The browser fetches them when the document is shown, which tells their server the document
  was opened. For private documents, pass a `resolveImage` that allows only your own hosts, or
  turn remote images off entirely:

  ```ts
  createEditorState({ doc, host: { resolveImage: () => null } }); // no image loads; the source shows
  ```

- Whatever you return, script-capable URLs (`javascript:` and similar) are dropped. See
  [Untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/).

## Pasting and dropping: `saveAttachment`

When the user pastes or drops an image, the editor calls
`saveAttachment(docPath, bytes, hint)` with the image bytes and a file-name hint. Store the bytes
and resolve the document-relative path to link; the editor inserts an image link to that path
where the image was pasted or dropped, with the caret in its alt text.
Resolve `null` when the save failed; the editor inserts nothing (report the failure yourself).

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const urls = new Map<string, string>();
let n = 0;

const state = createEditorState({
  doc: "",
  docPath: "/draft.md", // paste and drop need a document path
  host: {
    saveAttachment: async (_docPath, bytes, hint) => {
      const name = `attachments/pasted-${++n}.png`;
      urls.set(name, URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes.slice()], { type: "image/png" })));
      return name;
    },
    resolveImage: (src) => urls.get(src) ?? (src.startsWith("https://") ? src : null),
  },
});
```

This keeps images in the browser tab only. A real app uploads the bytes and returns the path or
URL it stored them under.

`resolveImage` may be called more than once for the same image, so keep it free of side
effects. When its answer changes, for example after the reader allows remote images, call
`editor.refreshImages()` and every image is resolved again, including those in tables.

## A document without a path: `uploadImage`

A CMS field, a comment box or a database row has no file path, so there is nothing to store an
image beside. Give `uploadImage(bytes, hint)` instead: store the bytes wherever you keep images
and resolve the URL or path to write in the link, or `null` when the upload failed.

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc: "",
  host: {
    uploadImage: async (bytes, hint) => {
      const res = await fetch("/api/media", { method: "POST", body: new Blob([bytes.slice()]), headers: { "x-name": hint ?? "image" } });
      return res.ok ? (await res.json()).url : null; // e.g. "https://cdn.example.com/media/42.png"
    },
    resolveImage: (src) => (src.startsWith("https://cdn.example.com/") ? src : null),
  },
});
```

Return a target that is valid in a Markdown link (percent-encode spaces) and that your
`resolveImage` accepts. When the document has a path and you give both, `saveAttachment` is
used.

The editor shows the new image by loading what `resolveImage` returns for that link, at once.
When the place you store it does not serve it yet, the image is broken in the editor until it
does: a CMS that keeps uploads in a draft store until the entry is published, for example, writes
`/media/42.png`, and that path answers 404 before publishing. Then resolve the link yourself:
keep what you uploaded, and have `resolveImage` answer from it first.

```ts
const pending = new Map<string, string>(); // link target → blob URL, until the server serves it

const host = {
  uploadImage: async (bytes: Uint8Array, hint: string | null) => {
    const path = await saveToDraftStore(bytes, hint); // e.g. "/media/42.png", not served yet
    if (path) pending.set(path, URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([bytes.slice()])));
    return path;
  },
  resolveImage: (src: string) => pending.get(src) ?? (src.startsWith("/media/") ? src : null),
};
```

After publishing, drop the entries (revoking their blob URLs) and call `editor.refreshImages()`.

## When an image cannot be stored

- With neither `saveAttachment` nor `uploadImage`, pasting or dropping an image inserts nothing.
- With only `saveAttachment` and `docPath` set to `null` (an unsaved document), there is nowhere
  to store beside, so the editor does not call it.
- In both cases the editor stays silent. To tell the user, pass `onUnsupportedPaste`: it is
  called with the reason (`"no-save-attachment"` or `"no-doc-path"`) and how many images were
  dropped.

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({
  doc,
  host: {
    onUnsupportedPaste: (reason, count) => {
      showToast(`${count} image(s) not added: this editor cannot store images.`);
    },
  },
});
```
- `hint` is the file's name, or its MIME type when it has no name. It is a hint, not a checked
  type: look at the bytes before you store or serve them.

## Resizing

Every image has a grip in its corner. Dragging it resizes the image, and on release the editor
writes the width into the alt text as `|W`:

```md
![diagram|320](diagram.png)
```

Only that width changes in the file. In reading mode the grip is hidden.

# Markdown syntax

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/syntax/

The editor reads CommonMark and GitHub Flavored Markdown, plus a few extensions: math, front
matter, image sizes, Mermaid diagrams and callout fold marks. Everything else is shown exactly as
written. It is never hidden or dropped, and the editor never rewrites your source to "fix" it.

The tables below are generated from the editor's test vectors, so they say what the editor does,
not what we hope it does. Each vector is checked on every test run.

## What the editor reads

"Rendered" means drawn in place, with the marks hidden when the caret is elsewhere. "Shown as
written" means the text stays as you typed it, with no special treatment.

### CommonMark

| Syntax | Example | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headings | `# Title` | Rendered | ATX (`#` to `######`) and setext (a line underlined with `=` or `-`). Headings get GitHub-style anchor ids. |
| Emphasis and strong | `*em* **strong**` | Rendered | `*` and `_`. The marks hide when the caret is elsewhere. |
| Code spans | `` `code` `` | Rendered | Nothing inside a code span is Markdown, dollar signs included. |
| Links | `[text](https://example.com)` | Rendered | Inline, reference (`[text][ref]`) and autolinks (`<https://…>`). A `[label]` with no definition stays text, brackets visible. |
| Images | `![alt](cat.png)` | Rendered | Local paths go through the host's `resolveImage`. See also image size below. |
| Lists | `- item / 1. item` | Rendered | Bullet (`-`, `*`, `+`) and ordered (`1.`, `1)`) lists, nested to any depth. |
| Block quotes | `> quoted` | Rendered |  |
| Code blocks | `` ```ts … ``` `` | Rendered | Fenced (with syntax highlighting by info string) and indented. |
| Thematic breaks | `***` | Rendered | Three or more `*`, `-` or `_` on a line of their own. |
| Backslash escapes | `\*not emphasis\*` | Rendered | The backslash hides when the caret is elsewhere and in reading mode, like other marks; the source keeps it. |
| Entity references | `&amp; &copy;` | Rendered |  |
| Raw HTML | `<b>hi</b>` | Shown as written | Shown as source text, never interpreted (see Untrusted content). |

### GFM

| Syntax | Example | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tables | `\| a \| b \|` | Rendered | With column alignment. Cells render inline Markdown and edit in place. |
| Task lists | `- [ ] todo` | Rendered | Clicking a checkbox changes only `[ ]` / `[x]`. |
| Strikethrough | `~~gone~~` | Rendered | Exactly two tildes. A single `~x~` is text (GitHub strikes it). |
| Autolinks (bare URLs) | `www.example.com` | Rendered |  |
| Alerts (callouts) | `> [!NOTE]` | Rendered | NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION, any case. |

### Extensions

| Syntax | Example | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Callout fold marks | `> [!NOTE]-` | Rendered | Obsidian's `-` / `+` after the type: rendered as the callout, nothing folds. |
| Inline math `$…$` | `$E = mc^2$` | Rendered | Pandoc's rules: a non-space after the opening `$`, a non-space before the closing `$`, no digit after it. One line. |
| Math `$$…$$` | `$$\int_0^1 x\,dx$$` | Rendered | On lines of its own: block math (may span lines). Inside a line of text: inline math, as in remark-math, Obsidian and Typora. |
| Math `\(…\)` and `\[…\]` | `\(x^2\)` | Rendered | The delimiters LLMs write. `\[ … \]` is block math when it is a paragraph of its own; on one line it needs a space inside both brackets. Otherwise these stay CommonMark escapes: `\[ … \]` in the middle of a line (sharing its paragraph with other text) is never math, by design, and shows as its text `[ … ]`, the backslashes hidden off the caret. (Pandoc's `tex_math_single_backslash` reads it as display math; the editor keeps CommonMark's reading there.) |
| YAML front matter | `---⏎title: x⏎---` | Rendered | At the very start of the file; shown as an editable Properties block. |
| Image size | `![alt\|300](cat.png)` | Rendered | `\|width` or `\|widthxheight` at the end of the alt text, in pixels (Obsidian's form). |
| Mermaid diagrams | `` ```mermaid `` | Rendered | A fence with info string `mermaid`. Off with `diagrams: false` and in the `no-diagrams` entry. |
| `@agent` mentions | `@agent(reviewer)` | Rendered | Coloured with `--ome-agent`; the text is unchanged. |

### Not supported

| Syntax | Example | Support | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wikilinks | `[[Page]]` | Shown as written | A host can style them with its own CodeMirror extension (see below). |
| Footnotes | `text[^1]` | Shown as written | Both the reference and the note. A note with no space in it is a CommonMark link reference definition, so `[^1]` links to it. |
| Highlight | `==mark==` | Shown as written |  |
| Fenced containers / panels | `::: note` | Shown as written | Read as a paragraph of text. |
| Subscript / superscript | `H~2~O x^2^` | Shown as written | Use math instead: `$H_2O$`. |
| Emoji shortcodes | `:smile:` | Shown as written | Emoji characters themselves are text and show as usual. |
| Definition lists | `Term⏎: definition` | Shown as written |  |
| Math fences | `` ```math `` | Shown as written | A code block (GitHub draws it as math). Use `$$…$$`. |

### How math delimiters are read

Each row is a test vector: the source, and what the editor renders it as (formulas as `<math>`).

| You write | It renders as |
| --- | --- |
| `$E = mc^2$` | `<math>E = mc^2</math>` |
| `$x$ and $y$` | `<math>x</math> and <math>y</math>` |
| `from $20-$30` | `from $20-$30` |
| `$1,000-$2,000` | `$1,000-$2,000` |
| `costs $5 and $10` | `costs $5 and $10` |
| `that is $5` | `that is $5` |
| `$ x$ and $x $` | `$ x$ and $x $` |
| `echo $HOME $PATH` | `echo $HOME $PATH` |
| `$HOME/$USER` | `<math>HOME/</math>USER` |
| `` `$HOME/$USER` `` | `<code>$HOME/$USER</code>` |
| `\$5 and \$10` | `$5 and $10` |
| `$a\$b$` | `<math>a\$b</math>` |
| `- $5 or $x^2$` | `<ul>⏎<li>$5 or <math>x^2</math></li>⏎</ul>` |
| `\| price \| formula \|⏎\| - \| - \|⏎\| $5 \| $x$ \|` | `<div class="om-table-wrap">⏎<table>⏎<thead>⏎<tr><th>price</th><th>formula</th></tr>⏎</thead>⏎<tbody>⏎<tr><td>$5</td><td><math>x</math></td></tr>⏎</tbody>⏎</table>⏎</div>` |
| `$$x^2$$` | `<math display="block">x^2</math>` |
| `$$⏎\int_0^1 x\,dx⏎$$` | `<math display="block">\int_0^1 x\,dx</math>` |
| `inline $$x^2$$ here` | `inline <math>x^2</math> here` |
| `$$x$$ then text` | `<math>x</math> then text` |
| `$$$x$$$` | `$$$x$$$` |
| `\(x^2\) inline` | `<math>x^2</math> inline` |
| `a \( x \) b` | `a <math>x</math> b` |
| `\(\) and \(a` | `() and (a` |
| `\[ x^2 \]` | `<math display="block">x^2</math>` |
| `\[⏎x = 1⏎\]` | `<math display="block">x = 1</math>` |
| `\[x\]` | `[x]` |
| `- \[x\] item` | `<ul>⏎<li>[x] item</li>⏎</ul>` |
| `\[ a \] b \[ c \]` | `[ a ] b [ c ]` |
| `Let \[ x^2 \] be the area.` | `Let [ x^2 ] be the area.` |
| `text⏎\[⏎x⏎\]` | `text⏎[⏎x⏎]` |

⏎ marks a line break.

## Math delimiters

Inline `$…$` follows [Pandoc's rules](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#extension-tex_math_dollars),
so prices and shell variables stay text: `$20-$30` is not a formula. To write a literal dollar
sign that the editor would otherwise read as math, escape it (`\$`) or put it in a code span.
`$HOME/$USER` outside a code span is a formula, as it is in Pandoc.

`$$…$$` on lines of its own is block math. Inside a line of text it is inline math, as in
remark-math, Obsidian and Typora.

`\(…\)` and `\[…\]` are the delimiters language models often write. They are on by default.
`\[ … \]` is block math when it is a paragraph of its own: put a blank line before and after it.
On one line it needs a space inside both brackets (`\[ x \]`); a bare `\[x\]` is CommonMark's
escaped brackets and shows as `[x]`. Where neither delimiter pair is complete, a backslash before
a parenthesis or bracket is an ordinary escape.

## Syntax your host adds

The editor has no plugin API for new Markdown syntax: its grammar is fixed, and `extensions`
cannot add parse rules or block renderers. What `extensions` can do is what any CodeMirror
extension can: decorate text. That is enough to style a host's own inline syntax, such as
wikilinks. This example is the one the package's consumer test runs in Chromium, WebKit and
Firefox:

```ts
import { Decoration, MatchDecorator, ViewPlugin, type DecorationSet, type EditorView, type ViewUpdate } from "@codemirror/view";

// Style [[wikilinks]] with your own class. The text stays as written.
const wikilinks = new MatchDecorator({
  regexp: /\[\[([^\[\]\n]+)\]\]/g,
  decoration: (match) => Decoration.mark({ class: "host-wikilink", attributes: { "data-target": match[1] } }),
});

export const wikilinkStyle = ViewPlugin.fromClass(
  class {
    decorations: DecorationSet;
    constructor(view: EditorView) {
      this.decorations = wikilinks.createDeco(view);
    }
    update(update: ViewUpdate) {
      this.decorations = wikilinks.updateDeco(update, this.decorations);
    }
  },
  { decorations: (v) => v.decorations },
);
```

```ts
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({ doc, extensions: wikilinkStyle });
```

Style `.host-wikilink` in your page, and handle clicks on it with your own DOM listener. Some
limits come with this:

- The decoration only adds a class. The editor does not know about it: copy as plain text, the
  HTML renderer (`renderHTML`) and reading mode treat the text as written.
- Replacing text with a widget (hiding the brackets) is possible in CodeMirror, but the editor's
  caret rules and copy do not know about your widget. We do not test or support it.
- Block syntax (`:::` panels, footnote sections) cannot get a renderer this way.

# Untrusted content

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/

The editor is built to render documents written by someone else, such as a teammate or an AI
agent. Rendering a document never runs its script:

- **Raw HTML is shown as source**, never rendered.
- **Math** (Temml, `trust: false`) and the editor's icons reach the DOM only through one sanitiser
  with an allowlist of elements and attributes. Unknown elements make the formula fall back to
  its source. Unknown attributes are dropped.
- **Mermaid** runs with `securityLevel: "strict"` and no HTML labels. Its SVG goes through the same
  allowlist.
- **Your own renderers** (`renderMath`, `renderDiagram`; see [renderers](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/)) go through
  the same sanitiser as the built-in ones: a formula must be MathML, a diagram SVG inside the
  diagram profile, or it shows its source.
- **Links** are classified the way a browser reads them, after decoding entities and removing
  control characters. `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `livescript:` and `data:` links are never passed
  to `openLink` or `openExternal`, however they are obfuscated. Your `refusedLink` is told
  instead.
- **Images**: without a `resolveImage`, only absolute `https:` images load. With one,
  script-capable URLs are still dropped.

## What stays your job

- **Network policy.** An `https:` image in a document is loaded by the browser, which tells its
  server the page was opened. If that matters, return `null` from `resolveImage` for hosts you do
  not trust, or proxy images.
- **Opening links.** `openExternal` and `openLink` receive URLs and paths the editor already
  classified as safe to follow; your policy still decides whether and how to open them.
- **Content Security Policy.** CodeMirror injects `<style>` elements, so a strict `style-src`
  needs a nonce through CodeMirror's `EditorView.cspNonce`, passed with `extensions`:

```ts
import { EditorView } from "@codemirror/view";
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({ doc, extensions: EditorView.cspNonce.of(nonce) });
```

What a strict policy (`script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`, no `'unsafe-inline'`)
needs, exactly:

- **The editor and math**: only that nonce. The editor writes no `style` attribute; a formula's
  styles are applied through `element.style`, which the policy allows.
- **Diagrams**: more. Mermaid draws each diagram once in the page to measure it, with `style`
  attributes and `<style>` elements that carry no nonce. Without
  `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` and `style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` the browser
  blocks them and reports violations. Either add those two directives, or pass
  `diagrams: false` to `createEditorState` (or import `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams`,
  which leaves Mermaid out of the build): `mermaid` blocks then stay code and Mermaid is
  never loaded. [Self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/#diagrams-and-the-policy) gives both policies,
  tested in a browser.

## Known advisories

`npm audit` reports one advisory in a fresh install; npm counts it as `3 low severity
vulnerabilities`, one for each package on the path (`katex`, `mermaid` and this package). We
assessed it, and it does not apply to the editor:

- **GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7** (low; `katex`, installed through `mermaid` 11): "KaTeX: Existing
  prototype pollution can bypass trust restrictions". Exploiting it needs a prototype pollution
  already present in the page *and* KaTeX output inserted without sanitising. The editor renders
  math with Temml, not KaTeX. Mermaid runs with `htmlLabels: false`, so its labels are plain SVG
  text. Every piece of markup the editor inserts goes through its one sanitiser, which refuses
  anything outside its allow-list. The fix exists only in Mermaid 12, which adds a dependency
  under a license this package cannot take (EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0). With the `no-diagrams` or
  `no-renderers` entry, neither Mermaid nor KaTeX reaches your bundle. Next review: 2027-02-04.

The release check fails on any advisory that is not assessed here.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately through the repository's GitHub security advisories, not in a
public issue.

# Math and diagram renderers

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/

The editor draws `$…$` / `$$…$$` formulas and ```` ```mermaid ```` diagrams through two
renderers. Each entry of the package carries built-in ones, loaded only when a document first
needs them, and you can give your own instead: your page's MathJax, KaTeX or Mermaid, so the page
loads one copy and every formula and diagram looks the same inside and outside the editor.

| Entry | Built-in formula renderer | Built-in diagram renderer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor` | Temml | Mermaid |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` | Temml | none |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-renderers` | none | none |

A renderer you give is used in place of the built-in one, with every entry. With no renderer at
all, a formula shows as its TeX and a mermaid fence stays a code block.

## Where they go

The renderers are two members of the editor environment, `renderMath` and `renderDiagram`, so
they follow its rules ([environment](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/environment/)): give them to every editor on the page with
`configureEditorEnvironment`, or to one editor with `createEditorState({ environment })`, and
replace them later with `editor.setEnvironment(...)`, which redraws every formula and diagram.

```ts
import { configureEditorEnvironment, createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

configureEditorEnvironment({
  renderMath: (tex, displayMode) => window.MathJax.tex2mml(tex, { display: displayMode }),
});
mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc: "Euler: $e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0$" }));
```

## Formulas: `renderMath(tex, displayMode)`

It receives the TeX inside one formula (without the dollar signs) and returns **MathML**: a string
holding one `<math>` element. `displayMode` is true for a `$$…$$` block. It is called
synchronously each time a formula is drawn, so hand it over once your renderer has loaded (after
`MathJax.startup.promise`, say). Throw on TeX it cannot render: that formula then shows its source
with the failure mark, and the rest of the document is unaffected.

- **MathJax:** `MathJax.tex2mml(tex, { display: displayMode })`.
- **KaTeX:** `katex.renderToString(tex, { displayMode, output: "mathml", throwOnError: true, trust: false })`.
- **Temml** (what the built-in one does): `temml.renderToString(tex, { displayMode, throwOnError: true, trust: false })`.

The browser lays MathML out itself, so formulas take your page's font and need no stylesheet.

## Diagrams: `renderDiagram(source, scheme)`

It receives the source of one ```` ```mermaid ```` fence and the editor's color scheme
(`"light"` or `"dark"`), and returns an **SVG** string, or a promise of one. Reject on a source it
cannot render. Pass the same function each time: results are cached per renderer, source and
scheme. With your page's own Mermaid:

```ts
import mermaid from "mermaid";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, type DiagramRenderer } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams";

let n = 0;
const renderDiagram: DiagramRenderer = async (source, scheme) => {
  mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: "strict", htmlLabels: false, flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }, theme: scheme === "dark" ? "dark" : "default" });
  return (await mermaid.render(`host-diagram-${++n}`, source)).svg;
};

mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc, environment: { renderDiagram } }));
```

The `/no-diagrams` entry plus your own Mermaid means your page holds one Mermaid, at the version
you chose, and the editor package never adds another to your bundle.

## What the editor does with the output

A renderer's output is placed in the page only after the editor's sanitiser has checked it, the
same one the built-in renderers go through (see [untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/)). The
TeX and the diagram source are the document's, so possibly someone else's.

- **Formulas** keep presentation MathML only. HTML layout (KaTeX's default output), SVG, links
  and styles make the formula show its source with the failure mark. Configure the renderer not
  to trust the TeX (`trust: false`; no `\href`).
- **Diagrams** keep SVG drawing elements, text and plain styling only, inside the editor's diagram
  profile. HTML labels (`foreignObject`), scripts, links, images and event handlers make the
  diagram show its source with the failure mark. Run Mermaid with `securityLevel: "strict"` and
  `htmlLabels: false`. The editor renames the SVG's root id (and every reference to it) into its
  own scheme; you need not.

## Code blocks

Highlighting fenced code is a third opt-in, the option `codeLanguages`: a list of CodeMirror
`LanguageDescription`s, matched by the fence's info string. The usual list is
`@codemirror/language-data`'s, about a hundred languages, each loaded the first time a fence uses
it. Install it beside the editor:

```ts
import { languages } from "@codemirror/language-data";
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const state = createEditorState({ doc, codeLanguages: languages });
```

Without `codeLanguages`, fenced code shows unhighlighted, and `@codemirror/language-data` (with
its twenty-odd language packages) never enters your lockfile. HTML inside Markdown is always
highlighted; its grammar loads the first time a document holds HTML.

# Server-side rendering

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/ssr/

Importing `@openmarkdown-dev/editor` does not touch `window` or `document`, so the package can be
imported by code that also runs on the server (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro and the like).
Every build checks this by importing the package in plain Node.

Mounting needs a DOM. Create and mount the editor only in browser code: an effect, an
`onMounted` hook, a client-only component.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

export function Editor({ doc }: { doc: string }) {
  const el = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const editor = mountEditor(el.current!, createEditorState({ doc }));
    return () => editor.destroy();
    // Mount once; see the React guide for pushing later changes in.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);
  return <div ref={el} style={{ height: 480 }} />;
}
```

## What the server can render

The server renders the empty parent element. If the page should show the document before the
script runs, render it yourself (as preformatted text or with any Markdown renderer) inside the
parent and clear it when the editor mounts.

## Bundle splitting

Math (Temml) and diagrams (Mermaid) are loaded with `import()` the first time a document shows
math or a diagram. Your bundler splits them into separate chunks; neither is in the first load
of a page whose documents have none.

# Self-hosting

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/

This guide is for pages that load JavaScript as plain files from their own server: a
server-rendered app (Jinja, ERB, Go templates, PHP) with no bundler of its own, or a site whose
policy rules out a CDN. You build the editor once with [esbuild](https://esbuild.github.io/),
copy the output next to your other static files, and load it with one `<script type="module">`
under a strict Content Security Policy.

If your app already has a bundler (Vite, webpack, Rollup, esbuild), you do not need this page:
import the package as in [your first editor](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/getting-started/first-editor/) and your
bundler does the same splitting.

## 1. Install

In a small build project (it can live inside your app's repository), install the editor, its
CodeMirror peers, the code-block languages (optional: highlighted fenced code) and esbuild:

```sh
npm install @openmarkdown-dev/editor @codemirror/state @codemirror/view @codemirror/commands \
  @codemirror/language @codemirror/lang-markdown @codemirror/lang-html \
  @codemirror/search @codemirror/autocomplete @lezer/common @lezer/highlight @lezer/markdown \
  @codemirror/language-data
npm install --save-dev esbuild
```

To build from a local package file instead of the registry (a tarball made with `npm pack`,
for example before a release reaches npm), install the file by its path. npm 7 and later install
the peers listed above with it:

```sh
npm install ./openmarkdown-dev-editor-0.1.0.tgz
npm install --save-dev esbuild
```

## 2. The entry

One module of your own imports the editor and mounts it. It reads the document from a
`<textarea>` your template fills, copies the document back into it on each change (so an
ordinary form post saves it), and hands CodeMirror the page's style nonce:

```js selfhost-entry
// src/editor.js
import { EditorView } from "@codemirror/view";
import { languages } from "@codemirror/language-data";
import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

// The nonce the server put in this response's CSP header, read from the page.
const nonce = document.querySelector('meta[property="csp-nonce"]')?.nonce ?? "";
const source = document.getElementById("editor-doc");

mountEditor(
  document.getElementById("editor"),
  createEditorState({
    doc: source.value,
    extensions: EditorView.cspNonce.of(nonce),
    // Render ```mermaid blocks as diagrams. Set false to keep them as code and
    // never load Mermaid; see "Diagrams and the policy" below.
    diagrams: true,
    // Highlight fenced code; each language is a chunk, fetched on first use.
    codeLanguages: languages,
    host: { onChange: (doc) => { source.value = doc; } },
  }),
);
```

## 3. The build

This script is the whole build. Run it with `node build.mjs`; it writes the editor into
`static/editor/`:

```js selfhost-config
// build.mjs
import { build } from "esbuild";
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const outdir = "static/editor";

const result = await build({
  entryPoints: ["src/editor.js"],
  bundle: true,
  format: "esm",
  // Mermaid, Temml and each code language become chunks, fetched only when needed.
  splitting: true,
  outdir,
  entryNames: "[name]",
  chunkNames: "chunks/[name]-[hash]",
  target: "es2022",
  minify: true,
  // Keep /*! … */ and @license comments in the file they came from.
  legalComments: "eof",
  metafile: true,
  logLevel: "warning",
});

// Every package that went into the output, with its license text, in one file.
const notices = new Map();
for (const input of Object.keys(result.metafile.inputs)) {
  const dir = /^(.*node_modules\/(?:@[^/]+\/)?[^/]+)\//.exec(input)?.[1];
  if (!dir || notices.has(dir) || !existsSync(join(dir, "package.json"))) continue;
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(dir, "package.json"), "utf8"));
  const file = readdirSync(dir).find((f) => /^(licen[cs]e|copying|notice)/i.test(f));
  const text = file ? readFileSync(join(dir, file), "utf8") : `License: ${pkg.license}`;
  notices.set(dir, `${pkg.name}@${pkg.version}\n\n${text.trim()}\n`);
}
const all = [...notices.values()].sort();
writeFileSync(join(outdir, "THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt"), all.join(`\n${"-".repeat(72)}\n\n`));
```

- `format: "esm"` with `splitting: true` keeps the editor's lazy `import()`s as separate files.
  Without splitting, esbuild would inline Mermaid and every language into one large file that
  every page downloads. If your page must load one file, see
  [bundling into one file](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/bundling/).
- `legalComments: "eof"` keeps the license comments some packages put in their code. Most
  packages do not, so the script also writes `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` with the license file of
