  every package in the output. Serve it, or link it from your app's notices page: the MIT and
  similar licenses require the notice to travel with the code.

## 4. What it writes

```text
static/editor/
├── editor.js                  the entry: the editor, CodeMirror and Lezer
├── THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt   the license of every package in the output
└── chunks/
    ├── chunk-….js             code shared between the entry and lazy chunks
    ├── mermaid.core-….js      Mermaid, loaded on the first diagram
    ├── flowDiagram-….js       one chunk per Mermaid diagram type (and so on)
    ├── temml-….js             Temml, loaded on the first formula
    ├── dist-….js              a CodeMirror language package
    └── ruby-….js, shell-….js  a legacy-mode language, one per language
```

**Deploy every file.** The entry and the chunks find each other by relative URL, and which
chunks a page needs depends on the documents it opens: a diagram type or a code language no
one has used yet still has to be there the day someone uses it. Copy the whole directory,
never a selection, and copy it again on every upgrade (the hashes in the chunk names change).

## 5. The page

The server makes a fresh nonce for every response, sends it in the CSP header and writes it
into the page. This is the strict policy. It is all the editor, its icons and its formulas
need; with `diagrams: false` in the entry it is all the page needs:

```text selfhost-csp
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-{{ nonce }}'; img-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'
```

A page that renders diagrams uses this one instead (see
[diagrams and the policy](#diagrams-and-the-policy)):

```text selfhost-csp-diagrams
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'nonce-{{ nonce }}'; img-src 'self' https:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'
```

```html selfhost-page
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>Notes</title>
    <meta property="csp-nonce" nonce="{{ nonce }}" />
    <style nonce="{{ nonce }}">
      #editor { height: 480px; }
    </style>
    <script type="module" src="/static/editor/editor.js"></script>
  </head>
  <body>
    <form method="post">
      <div id="editor"></div>
      <textarea id="editor-doc" name="doc" hidden>{{ doc }}</textarea>
      <button>Save</button>
    </form>
  </body>
</html>
```

- `script-src 'self'` is enough for scripts: the editor and all its chunks are files from your
  origin, and it runs no inline script and no `eval`.
- `style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'`: CodeMirror and the editor inject their styles as `<style>`
  elements, and `EditorView.cspNonce` stamps the nonce on them. The editor writes no `style`
  attribute: what a formula needs is applied through `element.style`, which the policy allows.
  Your own inline `<style>` needs the same nonce; `style="…"` attributes in your template are
  blocked by this policy, so put such rules in a stylesheet.
- `img-src https:` lets documents show images from the web. Narrow it, or drop it and pass a
  `resolveImage` to the host (see [images](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/images/) and
  [untrusted content](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/untrusted-content/)).
- The nonce sits on a `<meta>` element's `nonce` attribute rather than in its `content`, the
  same convention as Vite's: the browser hides the attribute from selectors, and the script
  reads it from the `nonce` property.
- Your template engine must escape the document it writes into the `<textarea>` (Jinja's
  autoescape does). Serve `.js` files as `text/javascript`.

## Diagrams and the policy

The editor puts a diagram on the page without inline styles: its `<style>` gets the nonce and
its style attributes are applied through `element.style`. Mermaid itself does not. To measure
a diagram, it draws it once in the page, setting `style` attributes and adding `<style>`
elements that carry no nonce. Under the strict policy the browser blocks those and reports
each one as a violation (about 36 for a flowchart). The diagram still appears, but its text may
be measured without its font settings.

Pick one:

- **Render diagrams**: send the diagram policy above. It is the strict policy plus
  `style-src-elem 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` and `style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`. A nonce cannot
  cover Mermaid's `<style>` elements, and browsers ignore `'unsafe-inline'` in a directive that
  also has a nonce, so `style-src-elem` lists none. Inline styles are then allowed on the
  page; scripts stay `'self'` only.
- **No diagrams**: set `diagrams: false` in the entry and keep the strict policy. A
  ```` ```mermaid ```` block shows as code, and the page never fetches Mermaid (its chunks are
  still in the output, unused).
- **No diagrams, and no Mermaid in the build**: import from the package's diagram-free entry
  instead, and keep the strict policy. Change one line of the entry, and drop `diagrams` (that
  entry ignores it):

  ```js
  import { createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams";
  ```

  `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` is the same editor with the same API, built from the
  same code, minus the diagram support: nothing it imports reaches Mermaid, so esbuild writes no
  Mermaid chunk and `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` does not list it. A ```` ```mermaid ```` block
  shows as code. npm still installs the `mermaid` package (it is a dependency of the main
  entry); it just never reaches your output.

## Native WebViews and static hosts

A desktop or mobile app that shows the editor in a WebView (WKWebView, WebView2, Android
WebView), or a site served as static files, has no server to template a page per response.
The build above is the same; four things differ.

- **Serve the files from an origin.** Module scripts and their chunk imports do not load from
  `file://`. Serve the output through a custom scheme (`WKURLSchemeHandler`,
  `WebResourceRequested`, `WebViewAssetLoader`) or a local origin, with `.js` as
  `text/javascript`. Chunk imports are relative, so they resolve against that origin.
- **Wait for the page, not for the load event.** A WebView can report the page loaded before
  the module graph has run, so the first call from native code finds nothing to call. Send a
  message as the entry's last statement and call into the page only after it arrives:

  ```js
  // last line of entry.js (WKWebView; use your WebView's bridge)
  window.webkit?.messageHandlers?.editor?.postMessage({ type: "ready" });
  ```

- **The nonce needs a server.** A nonce only protects a page when it is new for every response;
  a fixed one written into a static file protects nothing. Without a server, use
  `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` (what diagrams need anyway), keep `script-src 'self'`,
  limit `img-src` to the schemes your images come from, and set `connect-src 'none'` if the
  page needs no network. The strict policy above is for a server that sends a fresh nonce.
- **Only what is on screen is in the page.** The editor draws the lines in view and a margin
  around them, not the whole document; this keeps long documents fast. Anything that reads the
  page's DOM sees only that part: the WebView's own find, copying the rendered HTML, and
  screen readers and other accessibility tools. Read the text with `editor.getDoc()`, and for
  find use the editor's own panel (Cmd/Ctrl+F, or `editor.openSearch()`), which searches the
  whole document.

## Loaded on demand

The entry holds what every editor needs. The rest is fetched the first time a document needs
it, and never otherwise:

- **Mermaid** and the code for each diagram type, on the first `mermaid` code block of that type
  (never, with `diagrams: false`; not in the output at all, with the `no-diagrams` entry);
- **Temml**, on the first formula;
- **a code language's grammar**, on the first fenced block in that language.

A document with none of these downloads only the entry and the chunks it shares.

## Sizes

Measured with the build above on the 0.1.0 package (minified, before compression):

- the output is about 230 files and 5.3 MB on disk, almost all of it lazy chunks that most pages
  never request;
- an editor that mounts on a plain document fetches the entry and the chunks it imports, about
  720 KB;
- the first diagram adds Mermaid's core and that diagram type, about 760 KB for a flowchart;
- the first formula adds Temml, about 210 KB; a code language adds from a few KB to about 50 KB;
- a document with a diagram, math and a code language fetches about 37 files, 1.7 MB.

Built from the `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` entry instead, the output is about 125
files and 1.9 MB on disk: no Mermaid chunks. What a page fetches is the same as above for
documents without a diagram (the entry is the same size; a document with math and a code
language fetches about 9 files, 950 KB). The saving is in what you build and deploy.

Serve the files compressed (gzip or brotli); this JavaScript shrinks to roughly a third. The
chunk names carry content hashes, so chunks can be cached for a long time; `editor.js` keeps its
name and should be revalidated.

# Bundling into one file

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/bundling/

Some hosts bundle everything into one script: an esbuild or Rollup build with `format: "iife"`,
a plugin system that loads one file, a template that has one `<script>` tag. A one-file build
cannot leave anything for later, so every lazy `import()` in the editor is inlined into it: the
formula renderer, Mermaid with all its diagram types, the HTML grammar. This page says what that
costs for each entry and how to keep the file small.

If your bundler can split (Vite, webpack, Rollup or esbuild with `format: "esm"` and
`splitting: true`), you need only [first load with a splitting bundler](#first-load-with-a-splitting-bundler):
the renderers stay separate chunks, fetched only by a document that needs them.

## What each entry inlines

Measured by the release check: one minified IIFE that mounts the editor, with CodeMirror and Lezer
inside (your own copy of CodeMirror, if your page has one, is shared and not counted twice).

| Import | What is inlined besides the editor and CodeMirror | Minified | gzip |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor` | Temml, Mermaid and every Mermaid diagram type, the HTML grammar | 4270 KB | 1214 KB |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-diagrams` | Temml, the HTML grammar | 923 KB | 304 KB |
| `@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-renderers` | the HTML grammar | 721 KB | 246 KB |

The package's own code is the same in each. For a page that bundles into one file, use
`/no-renderers` and give the editor the renderers your page already has, or `/no-diagrams` when the
built-in formula renderer is welcome.

## First load with a splitting bundler

What a page loads before the editor appears, minified and gzipped with CodeMirror, is about the
same for every entry, but not for every bundler:

| Bundler | First load | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vite, Rollup | about 185 KB | The HTML grammar is split out and loads the first time a document holds HTML. |
| esbuild (`--bundle --splitting --format=esm --minify`) | about 250 KB | `@codemirror/lang-markdown` imports `@codemirror/lang-html` at its top level and calls it there. esbuild keeps that call, so the HTML, CSS and JavaScript grammars land in the first load. |

The esbuild figure is our measurement of a page that only mounts the editor (248 KB); an
integration measured about 262 KB for its own page. Formulas and diagrams stay separate chunks
with either bundler.

## The recipe

Import the entry without renderers, and hand it your page's own:

```js
// editor-live.js, bundled with esbuild --bundle --format=iife
import { configureEditorEnvironment, createEditorState, mountEditor } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-renderers";

configureEditorEnvironment({
  // The page's MathJax, already loaded: MathML for each formula.
  renderMath: (tex, displayMode) => window.MathJax.tex2mml(tex, { display: displayMode }),
  // The page's Mermaid: SVG for each diagram.
  renderDiagram: async (source, scheme) => {
    window.mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: "strict", htmlLabels: false, flowchart: { htmlLabels: false }, theme: scheme === "dark" ? "dark" : "default" });
    return (await window.mermaid.render(`diagram-${Date.now()}`, source)).svg;
  },
});

export function mountLiveEditor(parent, doc) {
  return mountEditor(parent, createEditorState({ doc }));
}
```

What the renderers must return, and what the editor does with it, is in
[math and diagram renderers](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/renderers/). Without them, `/no-renderers` shows formulas as TeX
and mermaid fences as code, which is a fine start for a wiki that has neither yet.

## Code blocks

Highlighted code blocks are an opt-in (`codeLanguages`), and what you pass is what gets inlined:
`@codemirror/language-data`'s whole list puts every grammar in the file. In a one-file build, pass
only the languages your pages use:

```js
import { LanguageDescription } from "@codemirror/language";
import { python } from "@codemirror/lang-python";
import { createEditorState } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor/no-renderers";

const codeLanguages = [LanguageDescription.of({ name: "Python", alias: ["py"], support: python() })];
const state = createEditorState({ doc, codeLanguages });
```

## No bundler at all

`@openmarkdown-dev/editor/browser` (`dist/browser.js`) is a prebuilt one-file ES module: the
`/no-diagrams` entry with CodeMirror, Lezer, Temml and the HTML grammar inside, minified (about
304 KB gzipped), opening with the license notices of what it bundles. Load it with
`<script type="module">` from your own server or a CDN that serves npm files, and give it your
page's Mermaid for diagrams. It holds its own CodeMirror, so it cannot take `extensions` built
from another copy; a page that uses CodeMirror itself should bundle the package instead
([self-hosting](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/guides/self-hosting/)).

It exports the editor's functions only, not CodeMirror's `LanguageDescription`, so it cannot take
`codeLanguages` either: fenced code shows unhighlighted. For highlighted code blocks, bundle the
package with the languages you want (the recipe in [code blocks](#code-blocks) above).

# Fidelity

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/

Lossless round-trip: open a Markdown file and save it without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was.

Most rich Markdown editors parse your file into a tree and write a new file out of that tree when
you save. That new file says the same thing in the editor's own style: your `_emphasis_` comes
back as `*emphasis*`, your `+` list as `-`, your setext heading as `#`, and some constructs, such
as frontmatter or callouts, can come back as something else.

This editor edits the text itself. What you typed changes, and the rest of the file stays as you
wrote it.

## The claim

This is the whole claim. Every sentence is backed by a test:

> OpenMarkdown edits your Markdown source text directly; it never rebuilds the file from a document tree. Open and save without editing, and the file is byte-for-byte what it was: line endings (LF / CRLF), BOM, final newline, whitespace, tabs, escapes and Unicode spelling untouched. When you edit, only what you touched changes, with a few exceptions, each pinned by a test: editing a cell of an aligned table re-pads that cell when you leave it, and widens that one column when the new text no longer fits; table commands change only the rows or column they act on, in the table's own style; indenting a list item or pressing Enter in a numbered list renumbers the affected items; Enter in a list item drops trailing spaces before the cursor; a file with mixed line endings gets uniform ones once you edit it; typing on a lone blank line between two blocks adds a line break after that line, so the block below stays separate.

The claim is about the file, so it holds when your host reads and writes the file with
`openMarkdownFile` and `saveMarkdownFile`. The editor keeps the document as a string in `\n` with
no BOM; these two keep what the string does not carry:

```ts
import { createEditorState, mountEditor, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const file = openMarkdownFile(bytes); // the file as read, a Uint8Array
const editor = mountEditor(document.getElementById("editor")!, createEditorState({ doc: file.text }));

const out = saveMarkdownFile(editor.getDoc(), file); // the bytes to write
```

- **Strict UTF-8.** Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 throw `InvalidUtf8Error` (its `code` is
  `"INVALID_UTF8"`). Refuse to open the file: a lenient decode would replace the bad bytes with
  U+FFFD, and the next save would write that damage to disk.
- **Unedited, the original bytes.** While `editor.getDoc()` equals `file.text`, `saveMarkdownFile`
  returns `file.bytes`: BOM, line endings (LF, CRLF, lone CR, or a mix of them), a missing final
  newline and Unicode spelling exactly as they were.
- **Edited, the file's conventions.** The BOM is written back if there was one, and every line
  break is written as the file's dominant ending (`file.ending`: the most frequent one; on a tie,
  the one that comes first). A file with mixed line endings gets uniform ones once you edit it.

A host that does its own decoding has to keep the same three rules for the claim to hold. The
OpenMarkdown app keeps them in its own (Rust) file layer. The
[save-load example](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/examples/) uses the two functions.

## Check it yourself

Run any Markdown file of yours through the package: open it, put it in an editor state, and save
it without editing. Save this as `roundtrip.mjs` and run `node roundtrip.mjs notes.md`:

```js roundtrip-check
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createEditorState, openMarkdownFile, saveMarkdownFile } from "@openmarkdown-dev/editor";

const bytes = readFileSync(process.argv[2]);
const file = openMarkdownFile(bytes);
const state = createEditorState({ doc: file.text }); // in the editor, no edits
const saved = saveMarkdownFile(state.doc.toString(), file);

console.log(Buffer.compare(bytes, saved) === 0 ? "byte-identical" : "changed");
```

For a UTF-8 file it prints `byte-identical` (other bytes throw `InvalidUtf8Error`, see above).
The editor's own test suite runs this exact script on every test run
(`src/editor/roundtripCheck.gate.test.ts` in the editor's repository), over a test file of valid
but unusual Markdown (`fixtures/roundtrip/`: setext headings, `+` lists, reference links, odd
YAML, unaligned tables, NFD Unicode, trailing spaces, tabs) and its CRLF, BOM, mixed line ending,
lone CR and final newline variants.

In a browser, the [live demo](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/demo/) shows the same thing: its
developer panel says `0 bytes changed` until you type.

## What the exceptions look like

Edit one cell of a table and leave it, and only that cell's line changes. A table written
compact stays compact, and so does a hand-compacted row in an aligned table. In an aligned table
the cell gets its column's padding back, and if the new text no longer fits, that one column is
widened: its other aligned cells get more padding, and the delimiter row gets more dashes, its
colons kept. Changing `10` to `1000000` in this table:

```diff
-| Plan    | Users | Price    |
-|:--------|:-----:|---------:|
-| Free    |   1   |       $0 |
-| Team    |  10   |      $29 |
+| Plan    | Users   | Price    |
+|:--------|:-------:|---------:|
+| Free    |    1    |       $0 |
+| Team    | 1000000 |      $29 |
```

Changing it to `12` changes the `Team` line only. Clicking into a cell and leaving without a
change writes nothing. Table commands (insert, delete or move a row or column, toggle a column's
alignment) change the rows or the column they act on, in the table's own style. Format table is
the one command that re-aligns a whole table. Nothing else in the file moves.

## Compared with other editors

We opened the same 56-line Markdown file in six embeddable editors (their npm packages, in
headless Chromium), saved it without editing, then changed one word and saved again:

| Editor | Open → save, no edit | Change one word → save |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **@openmarkdown-dev/editor** (CodeMirror 6) | byte-identical | only that word changed |
| **Atomic Editor** (CodeMirror 6) | byte-identical | only that word changed |
| Milkdown Crepe (ProseMirror) | 13 of 22 tracked features changed | the same 30 changed lines, plus the word |
| Toast UI Editor (ProseMirror) | 15 of 22 changed | the same changes, plus the word |
| Tiptap + `@tiptap/markdown` (ProseMirror) | 17 of 22 changed | the same changes, plus the word |
| MDXEditor (Lexical) | refused the file (reference links); 13 of 19 changed without them | the edit was lost on the full file |

Atomic Editor ties with us here, because it is built the same way: the source is the document.
The difference is with editors that rebuild Markdown from a tree. When we edited one table cell
(in 0.1.3, before cell edits stopped re-aligning tables), both CodeMirror editors re-aligned that table. Ours kept the column alignment. Atomic's rewrote
the delimiter row to `| --- |` and lost it.

The method, an example diff, the run date and the caveats are on [the method page](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/method/).

# How we compared editors

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/fidelity/method/

**Question:** if you open a Markdown file in an embeddable editor and save it, do you get your file
back?

**Run on 2026-11-04.** One test file (56 lines, 22 tracked features) went through six editors' npm
packages in headless Chromium, and we diffed what each one would save. The results include ones
that are bad for us; they are listed under [where OpenMarkdown did not win](#where-openmarkdown-did-not-win).

## The editors

| Editor | Package and version | Model | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenMarkdown | `@openmarkdown-dev/editor`, from source before its first npm release | CodeMirror 6, the source is the document | live-preview mode, no host |
| Atomic Editor | `@atomic-editor/editor` 0.6.2 | CodeMirror 6, the source is the document | defaults |
| Milkdown Crepe | `@milkdown/crepe` 7.22.3 | ProseMirror tree, serialized with remark | Crepe defaults (all features on) |
| MDXEditor | `@mdxeditor/editor` 4.3.3 | Lexical tree, serialized with mdast | headings, lists, quote, thematic break, link, link dialog, table, frontmatter, code block, image, Markdown shortcuts |
| Toast UI Editor | `@toast-ui/editor` 3.2.2 | ProseMirror tree, serialized with ToastMark | WYSIWYG mode, defaults otherwise |
| Tiptap | `@tiptap/core` + `@tiptap/markdown` 3.32.0 | ProseMirror tree, serialized with marked | StarterKit + TableKit + Markdown |

Every package was pinned to the newest release published at least two weeks before the run. All
six ran from npm in one Vite project, one page per editor, each loaded with its own Markdown import
and read back with its own export (`getDoc()` for OpenMarkdown, `getMarkdown()` for the others).
No public demo page was used.

## The tests

1. **Open → save.** Load the file, wait two seconds, then export with no input at all.
2. **One-word edit.** Double-click the word `quick` in a paragraph with a real mouse gesture, type
   `slow`, and export. The expected output is the file with only that word replaced.
3. **One table cell.** Click at the end of the cell `22`, press Backspace twice, type `23`, click
   into a paragraph to leave the table, and export.

**How a feature is scored.** Each of the 22 features is a verbatim snippet of the test file. A
feature counts as "changed" when that exact snippet is missing from the export. Each change was then
classified by reading the diff:

- **rewritten**: the meaning is the same and the syntax is different;
- **lost**: a GFM/CommonMark reader (or GitHub, for frontmatter and callouts) sees something
  different when the saved file is reopened.

## Results

| Editor | Open → save, no edit | Change one word → save | Then edit one table cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OpenMarkdown** | byte-identical; 0 of 22 features changed | only the word changed | the whole table re-aligned (4 lines); alignment colons and `\|` kept |
| **Atomic Editor** | byte-identical; 0 of 22 | only the word changed | 2 lines changed; the delimiter row became `\| --- \| --- \| --- \|`, so column alignment is lost |
| Milkdown Crepe | 13 of 22 changed (2 lost, 11 rewritten); 30 diff lines | the same 30 lines plus the word | only the cell changed, in its already-rewritten table |
| MDXEditor | refused the file: a reference link stopped its parser, and the edit never reached its export | edit lost | n/a |
| MDXEditor, file without reference links | 13 of 19 changed (4 lost, 9 rewritten); 34 diff lines | the same plus the word | only the cell changed |
| Toast UI Editor | 15 of 22 changed (8 lost, 7 rewritten); 40 diff lines | the same plus the word | only the cell changed |
| Tiptap | 17 of 22 changed (3 lost, 14 rewritten); 41 diff lines | the same plus the word | only the cell changed |

"Diff lines" counts the `+` and `-` lines of `diff -u`. For each tree-based editor, the one-word
output is its open → save output with one word changed: a one-word edit saves the same 30 to 41
changed lines that opening the file already caused.

## Example diff

Milkdown, open then save with no edit. The YAML frontmatter comes back as a horizontal rule and a
heading:

```diff
----
+***
+
 title: Round-trip corpus
-tags: [a,b ,  c]
----
+tags: \[a,b ,  c]
+-----------------
```

## Feature by feature (open → save)

`kept` means the bytes are identical.

| Feature (source) | OpenMarkdown | Atomic | Milkdown | MDXEditor¹ | Toast UI | Tiptap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| frontmatter `---`…`---` | kept | kept | lost: `***` + paragraph + setext h2 | kept | lost | lost: `---` + `## title: …` |
| `*stars*` | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| `_underscores_` | kept | kept | kept | rewritten `*…*` | rewritten `*…*` | rewritten `*…*` |
| `__underscores__` | kept | kept | kept | rewritten `**…**` | rewritten `**…**` | rewritten `**…**` |
| setext h1 (`====`) | kept | kept | rewritten `# …` | rewritten `# …` | rewritten, underline shortened | rewritten `# …` |
| setext h2 (`----`) | kept | kept | rewritten `## …` | rewritten `## …` | rewritten `---` | rewritten `## …` |
| table delimiter row | kept | kept | rewritten (padded) | rewritten (padded) | rewritten | rewritten (padded) |
| table row with `` `a\|b` `` and `\|` | kept | kept | rewritten (padding; escapes kept) | rewritten (padding) | lost: the bare pipe splits the cell on reopen | rewritten (padding) |
| unpadded table row | kept | kept | rewritten | rewritten | rewritten | rewritten |
| `[the spec][spec]` | kept | kept | rewritten inline | refused | lost: never parsed as a link | rewritten inline |
| `[Collapsed][]` | kept | kept | rewritten inline | refused | lost | rewritten inline |
| link reference definitions | kept | kept | rewritten (deleted, inlined) | refused | lost | rewritten (deleted, inlined) |
| `+` list marker | kept | kept | rewritten `*` | rewritten `*` | rewritten `*` | rewritten `-` |
| `*` list marker | kept | kept | rewritten `-` | kept | kept | rewritten `-` |
| two adjacent lists stay two | kept | kept | kept | lost: merged into one list | lost: one list on reopen | lost: one list on reopen |
| ordered list starting at `3.` | kept | kept | kept | lost: renumbered `1.` | kept | kept |
| backslash hard break `\` | kept | kept | kept | lost: soft break | lost: lines glued | rewritten as two trailing spaces |
| trailing spaces (a hard break) | kept | kept | rewritten `\` | lost: soft break | lost: lines glued | rewritten (2 spaces) |
| HTML block `<div align="center">` | kept | kept | kept | kept | lost: glued into the previous paragraph | lost: `**HTML block**` |
| inline math `$E = mc^2$` | kept | kept | kept | rewritten `$E \= mc^2$` | kept | kept |
| callout `> [!NOTE]` | kept | kept | lost: `> \[!NOTE]` | lost: `> \[!NOTE]` | kept | lost: `> \[!NOTE\]` |
| CJK paragraph | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| `\*not emphasis\*` | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept | kept |
| final newline | kept | kept | kept | dropped | dropped | dropped |

¹ MDXEditor values are from the run without the reference-link section. With the full file, it
reports a parse error on the reference link and renders nothing after it.

## Caveats

- **Atomic Editor ties with us.** It is also built on CodeMirror and edits the text itself. The
  split here is editing the text against editing a tree, not us against everyone.
- **Table edits:** editing one cell in OpenMarkdown re-aligns that whole table (4 lines in this
  file). Atomic changes 2 lines there, but drops the column alignment.
- **The test file is ours.** It uses valid but less common syntax on purpose: setext headings, `+`
  lists, reference links. A file written in one canonical style (ATX headings, `-` lists, `**`,
  padded tables) loses much less in a tree editor. A fair summary is "tree editors normalize your
  style and lose some constructs", not "they corrupt everything".
- **Configuration matters.** Each tree-based editor can be extended with more plugins; some
  community plugins (frontmatter, for example) could fix some rows. Rewriting `_` / `__`, setext
  headings, list markers and table padding is a property of serializing a tree, not a missing
  plugin.
- **"Lost"** means a Markdown reader sees something different when the saved file is reopened;
  **"changed"** includes harmless rewrites like `_a_` to `*a*`.
- **One run per editor, in headless Chromium.** Results were identical across every run made while
  building the test (six full runs).
- **Single gestures.** The edit tests do not cover typing-heavy sessions, paste, undo or IME input.
- **The editor alone.** OpenMarkdown was run from its source before the first npm release. The
  app's disk layer (BOM, CRLF) is not involved for this LF, BOM-less file; the editor's own
  fidelity tests cover it separately.

## Where OpenMarkdown did not win

- **The tie with Atomic Editor** on open → save and on a prose edit. Do not read these results as
  "the one editor that keeps your file".
- **Table edits** rewrite more bytes than Atomic's (4 lines against 2), by design.
- **`\|` inside inline code in a table** displays as `a\|b` in OpenMarkdown. GFM reads that cell as
  `a|b`, and Milkdown, MDXEditor and Toast UI display it that way. The bytes are kept, but the
  display is wrong.
- **Double-click inside a table cell** first opens the cell editor and places the caret, where the
  other editors select the word. The table test uses click and Backspace for each editor, so the
  numbers above are not affected, but a user would notice it.

The round-trip test file and the test that runs it are in the editor's repository
(`fixtures/roundtrip/`, `src/editor/roundtripCheck.gate.test.ts`). The comparison harness and its
per-feature results are not public yet.

# InvalidUtf8Error

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/classes/invalidutf8error/

Thrown by `openMarkdownFile` when the bytes are not valid UTF-8. Refuse to
open the file in the editor: decoding it anyway would replace the bad bytes
with U+FFFD, and the next save would write that damage to disk. Recognise it
with `instanceof`, or by `code` (`"INVALID_UTF8"`) across bundles.

## Extends

- `Error`

## Constructors

### Constructor

> **new InvalidUtf8Error**(`options?`): `InvalidUtf8Error`

#### Parameters

##### options?

###### cause?

`unknown`

The decoder's own error.

#### Returns

`InvalidUtf8Error`

#### Overrides

`Error.constructor`

## Properties

### cause?

> `optional` **cause?**: `unknown`

#### Inherited from

`Error.cause`

***

### code

> `readonly` **code**: `"INVALID_UTF8"` = `"INVALID_UTF8"`

Always `"INVALID_UTF8"`.

***

### message

> **message**: `string`

#### Inherited from

`Error.message`

***

### name

> **name**: `string`

#### Inherited from

`Error.name`

***

### stack?

> `optional` **stack?**: `string`

#### Inherited from

`Error.stack`

***

### stackTraceLimit

> `static` **stackTraceLimit**: `number`

The `Error.stackTraceLimit` property specifies the number of stack frames
collected by a stack trace (whether generated by `new Error().stack` or
`Error.captureStackTrace(obj)`).

The default value is `10` but may be set to any valid JavaScript number. Changes
will affect any stack trace captured _after_ the value has been changed.

If set to a non-number value, or set to a negative number, stack traces will
not capture any frames.

#### Inherited from

`Error.stackTraceLimit`

## Methods

### captureStackTrace()

> `static` **captureStackTrace**(`targetObject`, `constructorOpt?`): `void`

Creates a `.stack` property on `targetObject`, which when accessed returns
a string representing the location in the code at which
`Error.captureStackTrace()` was called.

```js
const myObject = {};
Error.captureStackTrace(myObject);
myObject.stack;  // Similar to `new Error().stack`
```

The first line of the trace will be prefixed with
`${myObject.name}: ${myObject.message}`.

The optional `constructorOpt` argument accepts a function. If given, all frames
above `constructorOpt`, including `constructorOpt`, will be omitted from the
generated stack trace.

The `constructorOpt` argument is useful for hiding implementation
details of error generation from the user. For instance:

```js
function a() {
  b();
}

function b() {
  c();
}

function c() {
  // Create an error without stack trace to avoid calculating the stack trace twice.
  const { stackTraceLimit } = Error;
  Error.stackTraceLimit = 0;
  const error = new Error();
  Error.stackTraceLimit = stackTraceLimit;

  // Capture the stack trace above function b
  Error.captureStackTrace(error, b); // Neither function c, nor b is included in the stack trace
  throw error;
}

a();
```

#### Parameters

##### targetObject

`object`

##### constructorOpt?

`Function`

#### Returns

`void`

#### Inherited from

`Error.captureStackTrace`

***

### prepareStackTrace()

> `static` **prepareStackTrace**(`err`, `stackTraces`): `any`

#### Parameters

##### err

`Error`

##### stackTraces

`CallSite`[]

#### Returns

`any`

#### See

https://v8.dev/docs/stack-trace-api#customizing-stack-traces

#### Inherited from

`Error.prepareStackTrace`

# configureEditorEnvironment

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/configureeditorenvironment/

> **configureEditorEnvironment**(`env`): `void`

Set the page's defaults (`EditorEnvironment`): what every editor uses for a
member its own `environment` does not give, and the page-wide UI
`language`. Call once at startup, before the first editor mounts; a later
call replaces the whole set. Optional: without it (and without a per-editor
`environment`) the editor is light, English, and has no clipboard,
external-link, spelling or host-key behaviour.

## Parameters

### env

[`EditorEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/)

## Returns

`void`

# createEditorState

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/createeditorstate/

> **createEditorState**(`options`): `EditorState`

Build an editor state: the document, caret, undo history, folds and mode,
with the whole editor (live preview, structure keys, find, folding, tables,
math, diagrams) installed. Show it with `mountEditor`; a host with several
documents keeps one state per document and swaps them into one view
(`editor.view.setState(state)`, then `editor.syncAmbient()`).

## Parameters

### options

[`EditorStateOptions`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorstateoptions/)

## Returns

`EditorState`

# mountEditor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/mounteditor/

> **mountEditor**(`parent`, `state`): [`MarkdownEditor`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowneditor/)

Mount `state` (from `createEditorState`) in a new editor view appended to
`parent`, following the environment's color scheme while it lives. Returns
the editor handle; call its `destroy` when done.

## Parameters

### parent

`HTMLElement`

### state

`EditorState`

## Returns

[`MarkdownEditor`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowneditor/)

# openMarkdownFile

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/openmarkdownfile/

> **openMarkdownFile**(`bytes`): [`MarkdownFile`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/)

Open a Markdown file's bytes for the editor. Decodes strict UTF-8 (invalid
bytes throw `InvalidUtf8Error`; nothing is replaced), notes and strips a
leading BOM, detects the line endings (LF, CRLF, lone CR, or a mix) and turns
them into `\n`, and keeps a copy of the original bytes. Save with
`saveMarkdownFile`.

## Parameters

### bytes

`Uint8Array`

The file as read from disk, a network response or a file input.

## Returns

[`MarkdownFile`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/)

The text to edit, and what saving needs to write the file back.

## Throws

InvalidUtf8Error when `bytes` is not valid UTF-8.

# openMarkdownText

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/openmarkdowntext/

> **openMarkdownText**(`source`): [`MarkdownText`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowntext/)

Open a Markdown file you hold as a string — a CMS field, a textarea, a JSON
response — for the editor: the same reading as `openMarkdownFile` after
decoding (notes and strips a leading BOM, detects the line endings and turns
them into `\n`), keeping the original string. Save with `saveMarkdownText`.
If you decode bytes yourself, decode with `ignoreBOM: true` (a default
`TextDecoder` drops the BOM before this sees it), or use
`openMarkdownFile` on the bytes instead.

## Parameters

### source

`string`

The file's content as a string.

## Returns

[`MarkdownText`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowntext/)

The text to edit, and what saving needs to write the string back.

# saveMarkdownFile

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/savemarkdownfile/

> **saveMarkdownFile**(`doc`, `file`): `Uint8Array`

The bytes to write for the editor's document. Unedited (`doc` equals
`file.text`), they are the original bytes, exactly. Edited, they are `doc`
encoded as UTF-8 with the file's BOM put back and every line break written
as `file.ending`; a file with mixed line endings gets uniform ones.

## Parameters

### doc

`string`

The document to save, usually `editor.getDoc()`.

### file

[`MarkdownFile`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/)

What `openMarkdownFile` returned for this file.

## Returns

`Uint8Array`

The file's bytes.

# saveMarkdownText

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/functions/savemarkdowntext/

> **saveMarkdownText**(`doc`, `file`): `string`

The string to store for the editor's document. Unedited (`doc` equals
`file.text`), it is the original string, exactly. Edited, it is `doc` with
the original BOM put back and every line break written as `file.ending` —
the same text `saveMarkdownFile` encodes.

## Parameters

### doc

`string`

The document to save, usually `editor.getDoc()`.

### file

[`MarkdownText`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowntext/)

What `openMarkdownText` returned for this string.

## Returns

`string`

The string to store.

# EditorEnvironment

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/

The editor environment: the capabilities that are not about one document —
the color scheme, the clipboard, external links, spelling, host keys and the
UI language. Give each editor its own with `createEditorState({ environment })`
(and change it later with `editor.setEnvironment`); `configureEditorEnvironment`
sets the page's defaults, which every editor uses for the members it was not
given. Per-document needs go through `EditorHost` instead.

Every member is optional: what the host leaves out is switched off quietly —
no error, no notice, no fallback of the editor's own — except the two
renderers, whose absence means the entry's built-in one. An editor mounted with
no environment configured at all is light, English, editable, and has no
copy, external-link, spelling or host-key behaviour.

## Properties

### colorScheme?

> `optional` **colorScheme?**: [`ColorSchemeSource`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/colorschemesource/) \| [`ColorScheme`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/colorscheme/)

Light or dark: a fixed `"light"` / `"dark"` (change it with
`editor.setEnvironment`), or a live source — its value now, and a
subscription to changes (returns the unsubscribe), which the editor
follows while it is mounted.

***

### copyText?

> `optional` **copyText?**: (`text`) => `unknown`

Put `text` on the clipboard (code-block copy button). The host reports success / failure itself.

#### Parameters

##### text

`string`

#### Returns

`unknown`

***

### handleKey?

> `optional` **handleKey?**: (`view`, `event`) => `boolean`

Offered every key the editor's keymap sees, before CodeMirror's defaults:
return true when the host ran a binding for it (the key is consumed).

#### Parameters

##### view

`EditorView`

##### event

`KeyboardEvent`

#### Returns

`boolean`

***

### language?

> `optional` **language?**: `"zh"` \| `"ja"` \| `"ko"` \| `"en"`

The language of the editor's own UI words. Read whenever a word is drawn,
so set it before the first editor mounts; already-drawn words do not redraw
on a change. Left out, or not one the editor ships: English. Page-wide
only: set it with `configureEditorEnvironment` (a per-editor
`environment` has no `language`).

***

### openExternal?

> `optional` **openExternal?**: (`url`) => `unknown`

Open an external (non-file) link target, e.g. Cmd/Ctrl+click on `https://…`. The host owns the policy.

#### Parameters

##### url

`string`

#### Returns

`unknown`

***

### refusedLink?

> `optional` **refusedLink?**: (`url`, `scheme`) => `unknown`

The editor refused to follow a script-capable link (`javascript:` /
`vbscript:` / `data:` …, however obfuscated); `scheme` is the
scheme as a browser reads it. For telling the user only: the URL MUST NOT
be opened. Absent: the refusal is silent.

#### Parameters

##### url

`string`

##### scheme

`string`

#### Returns

`unknown`

***

### renderDiagram?

> `optional` **renderDiagram?**: [`DiagramRenderer`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/diagramrenderer/)

Your own diagram renderer, used for every ```` ```mermaid ```` fence in
place of the editor's built-in Mermaid — for example your page's own copy
of Mermaid, so the page loads one, or to have diagrams at all with an entry
that carries no built-in one (`/no-diagrams`, `/no-renderers`). Left out:
the entry's built-in renderer, if it has one; else the fence stays a code
block. `EditorStateOptions.diagrams: false` turns diagrams off either way.
See `DiagramRenderer`.

***

### renderMath?

> `optional` **renderMath?**: [`MathRenderer`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/mathrenderer/)

Your own formula renderer, used for every `$…$` and `$$…$$` in place of
the editor's built-in one (Temml) — to draw formulas the way the rest of
your page does (MathJax, KaTeX), or to have formulas at all with an entry
that carries no built-in renderer (`/no-renderers`). Left out: the
entry's built-in renderer, if it has one; else formulas show as their TeX.
See `MathRenderer`.

***

### spell?

> `optional` **spell?**: [`SpellService`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/spellservice/)

The spell-checking service behind the editor's own squiggles and suggestions. Absent: no spell checking.

# EditorHost

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorhost/

What the editor calls back into, per document: pass it as `host` to
`createEditorState`. The editor reads each member through the object when it
needs it, so you can change the object later without rebuilding the state.

Every member is optional: a capability the host does not provide is switched
off quietly (no error, no notice) and the rest of the editor carries on.
Window-wide capabilities live in the editor environment
(`configureEditorEnvironment`).

## Properties

### getFolder?

> `optional` **getFolder?**: () => `string` \| `null`

The root folder of the user's files, for link-target completion. A getter,
read each time completion opens. Null, or absent: completion uses the
document's own directory.

#### Returns

`string` \| `null`

***

### listFiles?

> `optional` **listFiles?**: (`root`) => `Promise`\<`string`[]\>

The linkable files under `root`, as root-relative paths (link-target
completion). Absent: file completion offers nothing; heading completion is
unaffected.

#### Parameters

##### root

`string`

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string`[]\>

***

### onChange?

> `optional` **onChange?**: (`doc`, `isUserEdit`, `docPath`) => `void`

The document changed; `doc` is the whole new source. `isUserEdit` is true for
typing, pasting and other user actions, false for programmatic changes
(`setDoc`). `docPath` is the document the change happened in, so a host that
swaps documents can drop a change for one that is no longer shown.

#### Parameters

##### doc

`string`

##### isUserEdit

`boolean`

##### docPath

`string` \| `null`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### onMoved?

> `optional` **onMoved?**: () => `void`

The selection, scroll position or document moved (debounced); use it to remember the position.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### onOutline?

> `optional` **onOutline?**: (`outline`) => `void`

The heading outline changed; null when the view is going away (clear yours).

#### Parameters

##### outline

`Heading`[] \| `null`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### onUnsupportedPaste?

> `optional` **onUnsupportedPaste?**: (`reason`, `count`) => `void`

Images were pasted or dropped but could not be stored, so nothing was
inserted: `reason` is `"no-save-attachment"` (neither `saveAttachment`
nor `uploadImage`) or `"no-doc-path"` (only `saveAttachment`, and the
document has no path to store them beside); `count` is how many images.
Only a notice — the editor itself stays silent and the document is
unchanged. Use it to tell the user. Absent: nothing happens.

#### Parameters

##### reason

`"no-save-attachment"` \| `"no-doc-path"`

##### count

`number`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### openLink?

> `optional` **openLink?**: (`absPath`, `fragment`) => `void`

A link to a local file was followed (Cmd/Ctrl+click; a plain click in reading
mode): `absPath` is the target resolved against the document's directory, and
`fragment` its decoded `#fragment` without the `#` (`other.md#setup` →
`"setup"`), or null. The host decides whether the file exists, how to open it
and whether to go to the fragment. Absent: local links do nothing.

#### Parameters

##### absPath

`string`

##### fragment

`string` \| `null`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### resolveImage?

> `optional` **resolveImage?**: (`src`) => `string` \| `null`

Map an image target as written (`![](src)`) to a URL the page may load, or
null to show the source instead. Script-capable URLs are dropped whatever
this returns. Absent: only absolute `https:` images load. It may be called
more than once for the same image, so keep it free of side effects; when its
answer changes, call `editor.refreshImages()`.

#### Parameters

##### src

`string`

#### Returns

`string` \| `null`

***

### saveAttachment?

> `optional` **saveAttachment?**: (`docPath`, `bytes`, `hint`) => `Promise`\<`string` \| `null`\>

Store pasted / dropped image bytes beside `docPath`. `hint` is the file's
name, or its MIME type. Resolves the document-relative path to link, or null
when the save failed (report it yourself); then the editor inserts nothing.
Only called when the document has a path (for one without, see
`uploadImage`). Absent: image paste / drop stores nothing and inserts
nothing, unless `uploadImage` is given.

#### Parameters

##### docPath

`string`

##### bytes

`Uint8Array`

##### hint

`string` \| `null`

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string` \| `null`\>

***

### uploadImage?

> `optional` **uploadImage?**: (`bytes`, `hint`) => `Promise`\<`string` \| `null`\>

Store pasted / dropped image bytes wherever the host keeps images (an upload
endpoint, a CMS media library), for a document with or without a path.
`hint` is the file's name, or its MIME type. Resolves the link target to
write — any URL or path `resolveImage` will accept, valid as a Markdown link
target (percent-encode spaces) — or null when the upload failed (report it
yourself); then the editor inserts nothing. When the document has a path
and `saveAttachment` is given too, `saveAttachment` is used instead.
Absent (and no `saveAttachment` for a document with a path): image paste /
drop stores nothing and inserts nothing.

#### Parameters

##### bytes

`Uint8Array`

##### hint

`string` \| `null`

#### Returns

`Promise`\<`string` \| `null`\>

# EditorStateOptions

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorstateoptions/

What a new editor state starts with (`createEditorState`). Every field is optional.

## Properties

### ariaLabel?

> `optional` **ariaLabel?**: `string`

The accessible name of the editable text (`aria-label`), when no visible label names it. Default: none.

***

### ariaLabelledBy?

> `optional` **ariaLabelledBy?**: `string`

The `id` (or space-separated ids) of the element(s) that name the editable text (`aria-labelledby`). Default: none.

***

### checkSpelling?

> `optional` **checkSpelling?**: `boolean`

Draw spelling squiggles when the environment's spell service is on. Turn it
off for an editor where a squiggle could not be fixed. Default true.

***

### codeLanguages?

> `optional` **codeLanguages?**: readonly `LanguageDescription`[]

The languages fenced code blocks are highlighted in, matched by the
fence's info string — for example `languages` from
`@codemirror/language-data` (install it beside the editor), or a list of
your own `LanguageDescription`s. Each language's grammar loads the first
time a fence uses it. Default: none — fenced code shows unhighlighted.

***

### diagrams?

> `optional` **diagrams?**: `boolean`

Render ```` ```mermaid ```` fences as diagrams. With `false`, they show as
ordinary code blocks and Mermaid is never loaded — for a page that must not
download it, or whose Content Security Policy cannot allow Mermaid's inline
styles (see the self-hosting guide). Default true. With the
`/no-diagrams` and `/no-renderers` entries, which do not contain Mermaid,
diagrams render only through your own `renderDiagram` (environment).

***

### doc?

> `optional` **doc?**: `string`

The Markdown source to edit. Default: the empty document.

***

### docPath?

> `optional` **docPath?**: `string` \| `null`

The document's absolute path, or null for an unsaved one. Relative links and images resolve against it, and pasted images are stored beside it. Default: null.

***

### editable?

> `optional` **editable?**: `boolean`

May the user change the document? `false` makes the editor read-only in
every mode — no typing, pasting, dropping, task-checkbox toggling or
property editing, and no editing controls drawn; it can still be
focused, selected, searched and copied, and links still open. Live
preview then renders like reading mode. Change it with
`editor.setEditable`. Default true.

***

### environment?

> `optional` **environment?**: [`EditorOwnEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editorownenvironment/)

This editor's own environment: the color scheme, clipboard, external
links, refused-link notice, spelling and host keys for this editor only.
A member given here replaces the page's default
(`configureEditorEnvironment`); one left out falls back to it. Change it
with `editor.setEnvironment`. Default: none (the page's defaults).

***

### extensions?

> `optional` **extensions?**: `Extension` \| readonly `Extension`[]

Your own CodeMirror extensions, installed in this state beside the editor's.
They stay installed in every mode and travel with the state.

***

### fromState?

> `optional` **fromState?**: `EditorState`

Take over an existing CodeMirror state — from an editor this one
replaces — with its document, selection and undo history (the history
of `@codemirror/commands`' `history()`, the same copy of the package as
this editor's). Its other extensions are not carried over. `doc` and
`selection` are then ignored. Default: none.

***

### height?

> `optional` **height?**: `"fill"` \| `"auto"`

How tall the editor is. `"fill"`: the parent's height — give the parent
one; the editor scrolls inside it. `"auto"`: the content's height — the
editor grows as lines are added and the page scrolls, as a form field
would (a `min-height` on `.ome-root` keeps it from collapsing when empty).
Default `"fill"`.

***

### host?

> `optional` **host?**: [`EditorHost`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorhost/)

The per-document callbacks (change, links, images, attachments, completion, outline). Default: none.

***

### id?

> `optional` **id?**: `string`

The `id` of the editable text element, so a `<label for>` with that id
focuses the editor when clicked. Give the label's text to screen readers
with `ariaLabelledBy` (a `<label for>` does not name a non-form element).
Default: none.

***

### mode?

> `optional` **mode?**: [`EditorMode`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editormode/)

Live preview (default), plain source, or read-only reading mode.

***

### selection?

> `optional` **selection?**: `object`

Where the caret starts (UTF-16 offsets into `doc`). Default: the start of the document.

#### anchor

> **anchor**: `number`

#### head?

> `optional` **head?**: `number`

# MarkdownEditor

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowneditor/

A mounted editor (`mountEditor`): the CodeMirror view plus the operations a
host needs. Call `destroy` when the editor leaves the page.

## Properties

### view

> **view**: `EditorView`

The underlying CodeMirror view — the escape hatch for anything not covered here.

## Methods

### closeSearch()

> **closeSearch**(): `void`

Close the find panel and give the keys back to the text.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### destroy()

> **destroy**(): `void`

Tear the view down and drop the color-scheme subscription.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### docPath()

The shown state's document path, or null for an unsaved document (it travels with the state).

#### Returns

`string` \| `null`

***

### editable()

> **editable**(): `boolean`

Whether the user may change the document (it travels with the state).

#### Returns

`boolean`

***

### focus()

#### Returns

`void`

***

### getDoc()

> **getDoc**(): `string`

The current Markdown source, byte for byte what is being edited.

#### Returns

`string`

***

### isSearchOpen()

> **isSearchOpen**(): `boolean`

Is the find panel open?

#### Returns

`boolean`

***

### isUnedited()

> **isUnedited**(`file`): `boolean`

Is the document unchanged from `file` (what `openMarkdownFile` or
`openMarkdownText` returned)? The same test `saveMarkdownFile` uses to
return the original bytes: for an unsaved-changes indicator.

#### Parameters

##### file

###### text

`string`

***

### mode()

> **mode**(): [`EditorMode`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editormode/)

The shown state's mode (it travels with the state).

#### Returns

[`EditorMode`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editormode/)

***

### openSearch()

> **openSearch**(): `void`

Open the find panel and focus its field, as Mod+F does. It works in every mode.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### redo()

> **redo**(): `boolean`

Redo the last undone change, as Mod+Shift+Z does. Returns false when there was nothing to redo.

#### Returns

`boolean`

***

### refreshImages()

> **refreshImages**(): `void`

Ask the host's `resolveImage` again for every image, after its answer
changed (the reader allowed remote images, say). An image that resolved to
null showed its source; it now shows the picture if the new answer is a URL.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### revealText()

> **revealText**(`text`): `boolean`

Select the first occurrence of `text` (from the start of the document)
and scroll it into view, the way Find shows its current match — a match
in a table cell scrolls that cell in. The editor is not focused (call
`focus`). Returns false, and moves nothing, when `text` is empty or not in
the document.

#### Parameters

##### text

`string`

#### Returns

`boolean`

***

### setDoc()

> **setDoc**(`doc`): `void`

Make `doc` the document, for example after the file changed on disk. Only
the range that differs is replaced, so the scroll position, selection and
folds outside it stay where they were (an agent appending a line does not
move the reader). The same text does nothing. Not an undo step, and not a
user edit: `onChange` reports it with `isUserEdit` false.

#### Parameters

##### doc

`string`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### setDocPath()

> **setDocPath**(`path`): `void`

The shown state's document moved (rename) or was given a path (empty state → note).

#### Parameters

##### path

`string` \| `null`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### setEditable()

> **setEditable**(`editable`): `void`

Allow or forbid changing the document (`EditorStateOptions.editable`); document, selection and history are kept.

#### Parameters

##### editable

`boolean`

#### Returns

`void`

***

### setEnvironment()

> **setEnvironment**(`environment`): `void`

Replace this editor's own environment (`EditorStateOptions.environment`):
the members given override the page's defaults from now on, a new color
scheme applies at once. It travels with the state.

#### Parameters

##### environment

[`EditorOwnEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editorownenvironment/)

#### Returns

`void`

***

### setMode()

> **setMode**(`mode`): `void`

Switch between live preview, source and reading mode; document, selection and history are kept.

#### Parameters

##### mode

[`EditorMode`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editormode/)

#### Returns

`void`

***

### syncAmbient()

> **syncAmbient**(): `void`

After swapping a state in (`editor.view.setState(state)`): bring what is the
window's, not the document's — the light / dark half of CodeMirror's base
theme — in line with now. A parked state kept the value it had when it left.

#### Returns

`void`

***

### undo()

> **undo**(): `boolean`

Undo the last change, as Mod+Z does. Returns false when there was nothing to undo (or the editor is not editable).

#### Returns

`boolean`

# MarkdownFile

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdownfile/

A Markdown file opened with `openMarkdownFile`: the text to give the editor,
plus what `saveMarkdownFile` needs to write it back.

## Properties

### bom

> **bom**: `boolean`

Whether the file started with a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). An edited save writes it back.

***

### bytes

> **bytes**: `Uint8Array`

The file's original bytes (a copy of what was passed in).
`saveMarkdownFile` returns them as they are while the text is unedited.

***

### ending

> **ending**: [`LineEnding`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/lineending/)

The line ending an edited save writes: the file's most frequent one; on a
tie, the one that comes first in the file. `"\n"` for a file with no line
break.

***

### mixed

> **mixed**: `boolean`

Whether the file mixes line endings (two or more of LF, CRLF and lone CR).
Unedited, it is saved as its original bytes, mix included; once edited,
every line break is written as `ending`.

***

### text

> **text**: `string`

The text to edit: the file decoded as UTF-8, without a leading BOM, with
every line ending turned into `\n`. Pass it as `doc` to `createEditorState`
(or to `editor.setDoc`). Unicode is kept as written: nothing is normalized.

# MarkdownText

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/markdowntext/

A Markdown file opened from a string with `openMarkdownText`: the text to
give the editor, plus what `saveMarkdownText` needs to write it back. The
same as `MarkdownFile`, with the original string in place of the bytes.

## Properties

### bom

> **bom**: `boolean`

Whether the string started with a BOM (U+FEFF). An edited save writes it back.

***

### ending

> **ending**: [`LineEnding`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/lineending/)

The line ending an edited save writes: the most frequent one; on a tie, the first. `"\n"` with no line break.

***

### mixed

> **mixed**: `boolean`

Whether the string mixes line endings. Unedited, it is saved as it was; once edited, every line break is written as `ending`.

***

### source

> **source**: `string`

The string as it was passed in. `saveMarkdownText` returns it as it is while the text is unedited.

***

### text

> **text**: `string`

The text to edit: without a leading BOM, every line ending turned into `\n`.

# ColorScheme

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/colorscheme/

> **ColorScheme** = `"light"` \| `"dark"`

The editor's light or dark look; it follows `EditorEnvironment.colorScheme`.

# DiagramRenderer

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/diagramrenderer/

> **DiagramRenderer** = (`source`, `scheme`) => `string` \| `Promise`\<`string`\>

Renders one diagram's source (the body of a ```` ```mermaid ```` fence) to
an SVG string, in the editor's light or dark scheme; it may return a
promise. Reject or throw on a source it cannot render: the fence then shows
its source with the failure mark. Pass the same function each time —
results are cached per renderer and source. The source is the document's,
so run the renderer in its strictest mode (Mermaid: `securityLevel:
"strict"`, `htmlLabels: false`). Its output goes through the editor's
diagram sanitiser, which keeps SVG drawing elements and plain styling only:
HTML labels (`foreignObject`), scripts, links and event handlers make the
diagram show its source with the failure mark.

## Parameters

### source

`string`

### scheme

[`ColorScheme`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/colorscheme/)

## Returns

`string` \| `Promise`\<`string`\>

# EditorLang

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editorlang/

> **EditorLang** = *typeof* `EDITOR_LANGS`\[`number`\]

A language the editor's own UI words ship in (`EditorEnvironment.language`).

# EditorMode

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editormode/

> **EditorMode** = `"live"` \| `"source"` \| `"reading"`

How the editor shows the document: `live` renders Markdown in place and
reveals the source under the caret; `source` is the plain text, colored;
`reading` is rendered and read-only.

# EditorOwnEnvironment

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/editorownenvironment/

> **EditorOwnEnvironment** = `Omit`\<[`EditorEnvironment`](https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/interfaces/editorenvironment/), `"language"`\>

One editor's environment (`createEditorState({ environment })`,
`editor.setEnvironment`): any `EditorEnvironment` member but the page-wide
`language`. A member given here replaces the page's for this editor — given
as `undefined`, it switches the page's off; left out, the page's applies.

# LineEnding

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/lineending/

> **LineEnding** = "\\n" \| "\\r\\n" \| "\\r"

A line ending as it appears in the file: LF, CRLF, or a lone CR.

# MathRenderer

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/mathrenderer/

> **MathRenderer** = (`tex`, `displayMode`) => `string`

Renders the TeX inside one formula (without its `$` / `$$` delimiters) to
presentation MathML: a string holding one `<math>` element (MathJax's
`tex2mml`, KaTeX with `output: "mathml"`, Temml's `renderToString`).
`displayMode` is true for a `$$…$$` block. Called synchronously each time a
formula is drawn, so have the renderer loaded before you hand it over
(`editor.setEnvironment` redraws every formula with a new one). Throw on TeX
it cannot render: the formula then shows its source with the failure mark.
The TeX is the document's — possibly someone else's — so configure the
renderer not to trust it (no `\href`, no `\style`). Its output goes through
the editor's sanitiser, which keeps presentation MathML only: anything else
(HTML, SVG, styles) makes the formula show its source with the failure mark.

## Parameters

### tex

`string`

### displayMode

`boolean`

## Returns

`string`

# OutlineItem

URL: https://openmarkdown.dev/editor/docs/api/type-aliases/outlineitem/

> **OutlineItem** = `Heading`

One heading of the document, as `EditorHost.onOutline` reports it: its text,
level, line range and offsets.
